at padle.explanation: "At padle" means "to paddle". The tool you paddle with is "en pagaj" (a paddle). For example, "Jeg har glemt min pagaj" (I have forgotten my paddle). For rowing with oars, use "at ro" (to row) instead: "Vi roer over søen" (We row across the lake).

sentence.da: Vi kan **padle** hen over søen i en kano.
sentence.en: We can paddle across the lake in a canoe.

at pakke.explanation: "At pakke" means "to pack". When you put your things in a bag, say: "Jeg pakker tasken" (I am packing the bag). When you wrap a present, add "ind": "Jeg pakker gaven ind" (I am wrapping the present). When you mean a parcel, the noun "en pakke" is spelled the same: "Jeg henter en pakke" (I am picking up a parcel).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **pakke** min kuffert i dag.
sentence.en: I want to pack my suitcase today.

at pakke ud.explanation: "At pakke ud" means "to unpack". It is built from "at pakke" (to pack) and "ud" (out). When you take your things out of a bag, say: "Jeg pakker tasken ud" (I am unpacking the bag). When you open a present, it is also used: "Børnene pakker gaver ud" (The children unwrap presents).

sentence.da: Vi kan **pakke ud**, når vi kommer til hotellet.
sentence.en: We can unpack when we get to the hotel.

at parkere.explanation: "At parkere" means "to park". When you leave a car somewhere, say: "Jeg parkerer bilen her" (I am parking the car here). When you read a sign that forbids parking, you see the noun: "Parkering forbudt" (No parking).

sentence.da: Vi kan **parkere** bilen bag huset.
sentence.en: We can park the car behind the house.

at passe.explanation: "At passe" means "to fit (suit)". When clothes are the right size, say: "Skoene passer mig" (The shoes fit me). When a time is good for you, it means "to suit": "Mandag passer mig godt" (Monday suits me well). When you take care of a child, it means "to look after": "Jeg passer min lillebror" (I am looking after my little brother).

sentence.da: Bukserne er for store og vil ikke **passe** mig.
sentence.en: The pants are too big and will not fit me.

at passe børn.explanation: "At passe børn" means "to babysit". It is built from "at passe" (to look after) and "børn" (children). When you look after an animal, the same verb works: "at passe en hund" (to look after a dog).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **passe børn**, når I går i biografen.
sentence.en: I can babysit when you go to the movies.

at passe ind.explanation: "At passe ind" means "to fit in". When a person feels part of a group, say: "Han passer godt ind på holdet" (He fits in well on the team). When a thing looks right in a room, say: "Sofaen passer ind i stuen" (The sofa fits into the living room).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **passe ind** på min nye skole.
sentence.en: I would like to fit in at my new school.

at passe på.explanation: "At passe på" means "to take care or watch out". When you warn someone about danger, say: "Pas på!" (Watch out!). When you wish someone well, say: "Pas på dig selv" (Take care of yourself). When you look after someone's object, say: "Jeg passer på dine nøgler" (I am looking after your keys).

forms.en: I have taken care / watched out

sentence.da: Du skal **passe på**, når du krydser vejen.
sentence.en: You have to watch out when you cross the road.

at passe til.explanation: "At passe til" means "to go with or suit". When two pieces of clothing match, say: "Skjorten passer til bukserne" (The shirt goes with the pants). When a job is right for a person, say: "Jobbet passer til dig" (The job suits you).

sentence.da: Den røde jakke vil **passe til** dine sko.
sentence.en: The red jacket will go with your shoes.

at passere.explanation: "At passere" means "to pass". When you go past a place, say: "Vi passerer banegården" (We are passing the train station). To say you pass a test, use "at bestå" (to pass an exam) instead: "Jeg bestod prøven" (I passed the test).

sentence.da: Vi skal **passere** en lille by på vejen.
sentence.en: We have to pass a small town on the way.

at pege.explanation: "At pege" means "to point". When you point at something, use "på" (on) after the verb: "Han peger på bilen" (He points at the car).

sentence.da: Du kan **pege** på det, du vil have.
sentence.en: You can point at what you want.

at pege på.explanation: "At pege på" means "to point to". It is built from "at pege" (to point) and "på" (on). Danish keeps "på" where English says "to" or "at": "Han peger på bogen" (He points to the book).

sentence.da: Du skal **pege på** det rigtige billede.
sentence.en: You have to point to the right picture.

at pendle.explanation: "At pendle" means "to commute". When you travel to work every day, say: "Jeg pendler til København" (I commute to Copenhagen). A person who does this is "en pendler" (a commuter).

sentence.da: Hun vil ikke **pendle** to timer hver dag til arbejde.
sentence.en: She does not want to commute two hours every day to work.

at piske.explanation: "At piske" means "to whisk or whip". When you beat cream with fast strokes until it gets stiff, say: "Jeg pisker fløden" (I am whipping the cream).

sentence.da: Han skal **piske** æggene og sukkeret.
sentence.en: He has to whisk the eggs and the sugar.

at pjække.explanation: "At pjække" means "to skip school or play hooky". When you stay away from school without permission, say: "Han pjækker fra skole" (He is skipping school). Use "fra" (from) to name what you skip.

forms.en: I have skipped school / played hooky

sentence.da: Han vil gerne **pjække**, men han har en prøve i dag.
sentence.en: He would like to skip school, but he has a test today.

at placere.explanation: "At placere" means "to place". When you put something in a spot, say: "Jeg placerer vasen på bordet" (I put the vase on the table). When you give a guest a seat, say: "Jeg placerer dig her" (I will seat you here).

sentence.da: Du kan **placere** tasken ved døren.
sentence.en: You can put the bag by the door.

at plage.explanation: "At plage" means "to pester or torment". When a child keeps asking a parent for something, say: "Børn kan plage deres forældre om slik" (Children can pester their parents for candy). When pain or noise bothers a person again and again, say: "Smerterne plager ham" (The pain torments him).

sentence.da: Støjen fra vejen begynder at **plage** os om natten.
sentence.en: The noise from the road is starting to torment us at night.

at planlægge.explanation: "At planlægge" means "to plan". It is built from "en plan" (a plan) and "at lægge" (to lay). When you prepare a trip ahead, say: "Vi planlægger en ferie" (We are planning a holiday).

sentence.da: Vi skal **planlægge** festen, før gæsterne kommer.
sentence.en: We have to plan the party before the guests come.

at plante.explanation: "At plante" means "to plant". When you put vegetables in the ground, say: "Jeg planter tomater" (I am planting tomatoes). The noun "en plante" (a plant) is spelled the same. For example, "Jeg vander min plante" (I am watering my plant).

sentence.da: Vi vil **plante** et æbletræ i haven.
sentence.en: We want to plant an apple tree in the garden.

at pleje.explanation: "At pleje" means "to usually (do) or to care for". When you say what you normally do, put "at" (to) and the action word after it: "Jeg plejer at gå tidligt i seng" (I normally go to bed early). When you look after someone who needs help, it means "to care for": "Hun plejer sin syge far" (She cares for her sick father).

forms.en: I usually do / I care for
I used to / I cared for

sentence.da: Sygeplejersken skal **pleje** patienterne hver dag.
sentence.en: The nurse has to care for the patients every day.

at plukke.explanation: "At plukke" means "to pick", as in picking fruit or flowers. When you take apples off a tree by hand, say: "Børnene plukker æbler" (The children are picking apples). When you pull the feathers off a bird, it also means "to pluck": "at plukke en kylling" (to pluck a chicken).

sentence.da: Vi kan **plukke** jordbær i haven, når de er røde.
sentence.en: We can pick strawberries in the garden when they are red.

at plyndre.explanation: "At plyndre" means "to plunder or loot". When thieves or soldiers take everything of value from a place, say: "De plyndrer byen" (They are plundering the town). When someone takes all the food from a place, it also means "to raid": "Børnene plyndrer køleskabet" (The kids raid the fridge).

sentence.da: Tyvene vil **plyndre** butikken og tage alt af værdi.
sentence.en: The thieves want to loot the store and take everything of value.

at poste.explanation: "At poste" means "to post". When you put a message online, say: "Hun poster en kommentar" (She is posting a comment). When you send a letter, it means "to mail": "Jeg poster brevet i dag" (I am mailing the letter today).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **poste** et billede fra turen.
sentence.en: I want to post a picture from the trip.

at praktisere.explanation: "At praktisere" means "to practice", as in following a belief or working in a profession. To say what a person follows, say: "Hun praktiserer buddhisme" (She practices Buddhism). To say you repeat something to get better, use "at øve" (to practice) instead: "Jeg øver klaver" (I am practicing the piano).

sentence.da: Man skal have en uddannelse for at **praktisere** som læge.
sentence.en: You need an education to practice as a doctor.

at presse.explanation: "At presse" means "to press or pressure". When you squeeze juice out of fruit, say: "Jeg presser en appelsin" (I am squeezing an orange). When you push a person to do more, say: "Chefen presser os" (The boss is pressuring us).

sentence.da: Hun vil **presse** citronen over fisken.
sentence.en: She wants to squeeze the lemon over the fish.

at printe.explanation: "At printe" means "to print". When you print a page from a computer, say: "Jeg printer dokumentet" (I am printing the document). When a press prints books or newspapers, Danish uses "at trykke" (to print with a press): "De trykker aviser" (They print newspapers).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **printe** billetten før turen.
sentence.en: I want to print the ticket before the trip.

at prioritere.explanation: "At prioritere" means "to prioritize". When you decide how to spend your time, say: "Jeg prioriterer min tid" (I prioritize my time). When you decide where money goes first, it works the same: "Vi prioriterer pengene til huset" (We prioritize the money for the house).

sentence.da: Man må **prioritere**, når der er for mange opgaver.
sentence.en: You have to prioritize when there are too many tasks.

at producere.explanation: "At producere" means "to produce". When a farm or a factory makes goods, say: "Landmanden producerer mælk" (The farmer produces milk). When you talk about films or music, it also works: "Hun producerer film" (She produces films).

sentence.da: Fabrikken kan **producere** tusind biler om året.
sentence.en: The factory can produce a thousand cars a year.

at programmere.explanation: "At programmere" means "to program". When you write code for a computer, say: "Hun programmerer en app" (She is programming an app). When you set up a machine, it also works: "Jeg programmerer vaskemaskinen" (I am programming the washing machine).

sentence.da: Jeg vil lære at **programmere**, så jeg kan lave et spil.
sentence.en: I want to learn to program so I can make a game.

at protestere.explanation: "At protestere" means "to protest". When you speak out against something, add "mod" (against): "Folk protesterer mod den nye lov" (People protest against the new law).

sentence.da: Mange mennesker vil **protestere** mod de høje priser.
sentence.en: Many people will protest against the high prices.

at præsentere.explanation: "At præsentere" means "to present or introduce". When you introduce one person to another, add "for" (to) before the second person: "Jeg præsenterer min ven for min mor" (I introduce my friend to my mom). When you show a plan to a group, it means "to present": "Hun præsenterer projektet for chefen" (She presents the project to the boss).

sentence.da: Må jeg **præsentere** min kone for dig?
sentence.en: May I introduce my wife to you?

at prøve.explanation: "At prøve" means "to try". When you test something new, say: "Jeg prøver sushi" (I am trying sushi). When you put on clothes to see how they look, it means "to try on": "Hun prøver en kjole" (She is trying on a dress). The noun "en prøve" (a test) is spelled the same. For example, "Vi har en prøve i dag" (We have a test today).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **prøve** at tale dansk.
sentence.en: I want to try to speak Danish.

at prøve på.explanation: "At prøve på" means "to try to". When you say you are making an effort to do something, say: "Jeg prøver på at sove" (I am trying to sleep). The meaning stays the same without "på" (on). For example, "Jeg prøver at sove" (I am trying to sleep).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **prøve på** at lære flere danske ord.
sentence.en: I will try to learn more Danish words.

at prøve tøj.explanation: "At prøve tøj" means "to try on clothes". It is built from "at prøve" (to try) and "tøj" (clothes). When you ask a shop assistant for permission, say: "Må jeg prøve denne trøje?" (May I try on this sweater?).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **prøve tøj** i butikken.
sentence.en: I would like to try on clothes in the store.

at pudse.explanation: "At pudse" means "to polish". When you rub a thing until it shines, say: "Jeg pudser sølvet" (I am polishing the silver). When you clean glass, it also means "to clean windows": "Jeg pudser vinduer" (I am cleaning windows).

sentence.da: Han vil **pudse** skoene, fordi de er matte.
sentence.en: He wants to polish the shoes because they are dull.

at puste.explanation: "At puste" means "to blow or puff". When you fill a balloon with air, add "op" (up): "Han puster en ballon op" (He blows up a balloon). When you rest after hard effort, use "at puste ud" (to breathe out): "Jeg puster ud efter løbeturen" (I am catching my breath after the run).

sentence.da: Han skal **puste** på suppen, fordi den er varm.
sentence.en: He has to blow on the soup because it is hot.

at putte.explanation: "At putte" means "to put". When you slip something into a pocket or a bag, say: "Jeg putter bogen i tasken" (I put the book in the bag). When you put a child to bed, it also means "to tuck in": "Jeg putter børnene" (I am tucking the children in).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **putte** nøglerne i min lomme.
sentence.en: I want to put the keys in my pocket.

at pynte.explanation: "At pynte" means "to decorate". When you make a room look festive, say: "Vi pynter juletræet" (We are decorating the Christmas tree). With "sig" (oneself) it means "to dress up". For example, "Hun pyntede sig til festen" (She dressed up for the party).

sentence.da: Vi vil **pynte** stuen til festen i morgen.
sentence.en: We want to decorate the living room for the party tomorrow.

at påberåbe sig.explanation: "At påberåbe sig" means "to invoke". When you name a right as your reason, say: "Han påberåber sig sin ret til ferie" (He invokes his right to a holiday). The word "sig" (oneself) changes with the person. For example, "du påberåber dig" (you invoke).

sentence.da: Hun kan **påberåbe sig** loven, når chefen ikke overholder aftalen.
sentence.en: She can invoke the law when the boss does not keep the agreement.

at pådrage sig.explanation: "At pådrage sig" means "to catch or incur". When you get an illness, say: "Hun pådrog sig en forkølelse" (She caught a cold). When you run up debt, say: "Han pådrager sig gæld" (He is running up debt).

sentence.da: Hun kan **pådrage sig** en skade, når hun løber på is.
sentence.en: She can pick up an injury when she runs on ice.

at påføre.explanation: "At påføre" means "to inflict or apply". When you cause pain to someone, say: "Han påfører hende smerte" (He inflicts pain on her). When you put a layer onto skin, say: "Jeg påfører solcreme" (I apply sunscreen). To say you catch something yourself, use "at pådrage sig" (to catch) instead: "Hun pådrager sig en forkølelse" (She catches a cold).

sentence.da: Stormen kan **påføre** byen store skader.
sentence.en: The storm can inflict great damage on the town.

at pålægge.explanation: "At pålægge" means "to impose". It is built from "på" (on) and "at lægge" (to lay), like "pålæg" (sandwich toppings). When a boss gives people extra duties, say: "Chefen pålægger medarbejderne ekstra arbejde" (The boss imposes extra work on the employees).

sentence.da: Staten vil **pålægge** bilerne en ny afgift.
sentence.en: The state wants to impose a new tax on cars.

at påpege.explanation: "At påpege" means "to point out". When you tell someone about a mistake, say: "Jeg påpeger en fejl" (I point out a mistake). To point with your finger, use "at pege" (to point) instead: "Hun peger på døren" (She points at the door).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **påpege** fejlene i opgaven, og vi retter dem.
sentence.en: The teacher will point out the mistakes in the assignment, and we fix them.

at påstå.explanation: "At påstå" means "to claim". When you repeat what someone says is true, put "at" (that) after it: "Han påstår, at han ikke vidste det" (He claims that he did not know). The noun is "en påstand" (a claim).

sentence.da: Hvordan kan du **påstå**, at du aldrig har set den?
sentence.en: How can you claim that you have never seen it?

at påtage sig.explanation: "At påtage sig" means "to take on". When you accept a duty, say: "Han påtager sig ansvaret" (He takes on the responsibility). The word "sig" (oneself) changes with the person. For example, "du påtager dig" (you take on).

sentence.da: Hun vil **påtage sig** opgaven, fordi ingen andre har tid.
sentence.en: She will take on the task because nobody else has time.

at påvirke.explanation: "At påvirke" means "to influence". When you say one person changes another, say: "Vennerne påvirker hende" (Her friends influence her). When someone has drunk too much, it also means "under the influence": "Han er påvirket af alkohol" (He is under the influence of alcohol).

sentence.da: Dårlig søvn kan **påvirke** dit humør og din hukommelse.
sentence.en: Bad sleep can influence your mood and your memory.

en p-plads.explanation: "En p-plads" means "a parking spot". The "p" stands for "parkering" (parking), and "plads" means "space". When you say you have room for cars, say: "Vi har to p-pladser" (We have two parking spots).

sentence.da: Hvert hus har en **p-plads** til bilen.
sentence.en: Every house has a parking spot for the car.

en p-skive.explanation: "En p-skive" means "a parking disc". It is built from "p" (parking) and "en skive" (a disc). When you set the arrival time on it, say: "Jeg stiller p-skiven til klokken ni" (I set the parking disc to nine o'clock).

sentence.da: Husk at lægge en **p-skive** bag forruden.
sentence.en: Remember to put a parking disc behind the windshield.

en pakke.explanation: "En pakke" means "a package". When you get something in the mail, say: "Jeg har fået en pakke" (I have received a package). When you buy butter or tea, it also means "a packet": "en pakke smør" (a packet of butter).

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **pakke** med posten i dag.
sentence.en: I got a package in the mail today.

en pakkeboks.explanation: "En pakkeboks" means "a parcel locker". It is built from "en pakke" (a parcel) and "en boks" (a box). When you say where your parcel is, say: "Pakken ligger i pakkeboksen" (The parcel is in the parcel locker).

sentence.da: Jeg henter pakken i en **pakkeboks** ved stationen.
sentence.en: I pick up the parcel from a parcel locker by the station.

en pakkekalender.explanation: "En pakkekalender" means "a gift Advent calendar". It is built from "en pakke" (a package) and "en kalender" (a calendar). In Denmark it holds 24 small wrapped presents, one for each day until Christmas Eve.

sentence.da: Børnene åbner en pakke i deres **pakkekalender** hver morgen i december.
sentence.en: The children open a package in their gift Advent calendar every morning in December.

en pakkeshop.explanation: "En pakkeshop" means "a parcel shop". It is built from "en pakke" (a parcel) and "shop" (shop). To say you collect a parcel from a locker instead, use "en pakkeboks" (a parcel locker): "Jeg henter pakken i en pakkeboks" (I am collecting the parcel from a parcel locker).

sentence.da: Jeg henter min pakke i en **pakkeshop** i dag.
sentence.en: I pick up my parcel at a parcel shop today.

en pande.explanation: "En pande" means "a pan". When you mean the front of your head, the same word means "forehead": "Han har ondt i panden" (He has a pain in his forehead).

sentence.da: Jeg steger æg på en varm **pande**.
sentence.en: I fry eggs in a hot pan.

en pandekage.explanation: "En pandekage" means "a pancake". It is built from "en pande" (a pan) and "en kage" (a cake). To say what goes with it, use "med" (with): "pandekager med syltetøj" (pancakes with jam).

sentence.da: Jeg steger en **pandekage** på en pande.
sentence.en: I fry a pancake in a pan.

en pandemi.explanation: "En pandemi" means "a pandemic". To say a disease spreads in only one area, use "en epidemi" (an epidemic) instead: "Der er en epidemi i byen" (There is an epidemic in the city).

sentence.da: Under en **pandemi** bliver mange skoler lukket, og folk arbejder hjemmefra.
sentence.en: During a pandemic many schools are closed, and people work from home.

en pantautomat.explanation: "En pantautomat" means "a bottle return machine". It is built from "pant" (deposit) and "en automat" (a machine). In Denmark you pay a deposit on bottles and cans, and the machine gives the money back when you return them.

sentence.da: Jeg afleverer tomme flasker i en **pantautomat**.
sentence.en: I return empty bottles in a bottle return machine.

en pantbon.explanation: "En pantbon" means "a deposit receipt". It is built from "pant" (deposit) and "en bon" (a slip). In Denmark the cashier takes the amount off your shopping when you hand it in.

sentence.da: Jeg afleverer min **pantbon** i kassen.
sentence.en: I hand in my deposit receipt at the checkout.

en papegøje.explanation: "En papegøje" means "a parrot". English speakers should spell the ending with "ø", as in "papegøje". To say where a pet bird sits, say: "Papegøjen sidder i et bur" (The parrot is sitting in a cage).

sentence.da: Vores **papegøje** kan sige hej.
sentence.en: Our parrot can say hello.

en papirclips.explanation: "En papirclips" means "a paper clip". It is built from "papir" (paper) and "clips", an English word that Danish borrowed. To say you hold sheets together, say: "Sæt en papirclips på arkene" (Put a paper clip on the sheets).

sentence.da: Jeg samler arkene med en **papirclips**, men du kan også bruge en hæftemaskine.
sentence.en: I put the sheets together with a paper clip, but you can also use a stapler.

en papirkurv.explanation: "En papirkurv" means "a wastepaper basket". It is built from "papir" (paper) and "en kurv" (a basket). To tell someone to throw paper away, say: "Smid papiret i papirkurven" (Throw the paper in the wastepaper basket).

sentence.da: Ved skrivebordet står en **papirkurv** til brugt papir.
sentence.en: By the desk there is a wastepaper basket for used paper.

en paraply.explanation: "En paraply" means "an umbrella". To remind someone to take it when it rains, say: "Husk din paraply" (Remember your umbrella). For sun, use "en parasol" (a sunshade) instead: "Vi sidder under en parasol" (We sit under a sunshade).

sentence.da: Det regner, så jeg bruger en **paraply**.
sentence.en: It is raining, so I use an umbrella.

en parasol.explanation: "En parasol" means "a parasol". For rain, use "en paraply" (an umbrella) instead: "Det regner, så jeg tager en paraply med" (It is raining, so I take an umbrella along).

sentence.da: Vi sidder i skyggen under en **parasol**.
sentence.en: We sit in the shade under a parasol.

en parfume.explanation: "En parfume" means "a perfume". English speakers should spell it with "a" in the middle, not "e": "parfume". To say how much you have, use "en flaske" (a bottle): "en flaske parfume" (a bottle of perfume).

sentence.da: Hun sprøjter **parfume** på halsen.
sentence.en: She sprays perfume on her neck.

en park.explanation: "En park" means "a park". A private plot behind a house is "en have" (a garden), not "en park". For example, "Vi sidder i haven bag huset" (We are sitting in the garden behind the house).

sentence.da: Vi går en tur i en **park**.
sentence.en: We go for a walk in a park.

en parkeringsautomat.explanation: "En parkeringsautomat" means "a parking meter". It is built from "parkering" (parking) and "en automat" (a machine). To say where you pay, say: "Jeg betaler ved parkeringsautomaten" (I pay at the parking meter).

sentence.da: Ved gaden står en **parkeringsautomat**, og den tager kun kort.
sentence.en: By the street there is a parking meter, and it only takes cards.

en parkeringsbøde.explanation: "En parkeringsbøde" means "a parking ticket". It is built from "parkering" (parking) and "en bøde" (a fine). To say you pay it, say: "Jeg betaler parkeringsbøden" (I am paying the parking ticket).

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **parkeringsbøde** foran butikken.
sentence.en: I got a parking ticket in front of the shop.

en parkeringsplads.explanation: "En parkeringsplads" means "a parking space or lot". It is built from "parkering" (parking) and "en plads" (a space). The short form is "en p-plads" (a parking spot). For example, "Der er ingen ledig p-plads" (There is no free parking spot).

sentence.da: Bilerne holder på en stor **parkeringsplads** ved butikken.
sentence.en: The cars are parked in a big parking lot by the store.

en parkeringsvagt.explanation: "En parkeringsvagt" means "a parking attendant". It is built from "parkering" (parking) and "en vagt" (a guard). To say what the attendant does, say: "Parkeringsvagten giver mig en bøde" (The parking attendant gives me a fine).

sentence.da: En **parkeringsvagt** går rundt og tjekker bilerne.
sentence.en: A parking attendant walks around and checks the cars.

en parodi.explanation: "En parodi" means "a parody". When you name what is copied, use "på" (on) after it: "Showet er en parodi på nyhederne" (The show is a parody of the news). English speakers should spell the ending with "i", not "y": "parodi".

sentence.da: Filmen er en **parodi** på gamle gyserfilm og får alle til at grine.
sentence.en: The film is a parody of old horror films and makes everyone laugh.

en partner.explanation: "En partner" means "a partner". When you talk about the person you live with, say: "Min partner og jeg bor i København" (My partner and I live in Copenhagen). When you talk about a co-owner of a firm, it also works: "Jeg er partner i et firma" (I am a partner in a firm).

sentence.da: Min **partner** og jeg bor i København.
sentence.en: My partner and I live in Copenhagen.

en passager.explanation: "En passager" means "a passenger". To say you ride along but do not drive, say: "Jeg er passager i bilen" (I am a passenger in the car).

sentence.da: Hver **passager** skal have en billet.
sentence.en: Every passenger has to have a ticket.

en passagerfærge.explanation: "En passagerfærge" means "a passenger ferry". It is built from "en passager" (a passenger) and "en færge" (a ferry). The first part also appears in "et passagerfly" (a passenger plane).

sentence.da: Der sejler en **passagerfærge** til øen hver time.
sentence.en: A passenger ferry sails to the island every hour.

en pastor.explanation: "En pastor" means "a pastor". When you name a pastor, put "pastor" before the name: "Pastor Hansen holder gudstjeneste" (Pastor Hansen leads the service). The common word for a priest of the Danish church is "en præst" (a priest). For example, "Præsten døber barnet" (The priest baptizes the child).

sentence.da: Vores **pastor** holder gudstjeneste hver søndag klokken ti.
sentence.en: Our pastor holds a service every Sunday at ten o'clock.

en patient.explanation: "En patient" means "a patient", as in a person who receives medical care. The English word "patient" meaning calm is "tålmodig" in Danish. For example, "Han er tålmodig" (He is patient).

sentence.da: Lægen hjælper en syg **patient** på sygehuset.
sentence.en: The doctor helps a sick patient at the hospital.

en patrulje.explanation: "En patrulje" means "a patrol". To say a group goes out to watch an area, say: "Politiet sender en patrulje" (The police send out a patrol).

sentence.da: En **patrulje** går rundt i området hver nat og holder øje med folk.
sentence.en: A patrol walks around the area every night and keeps an eye on people.

en pause.explanation: "En pause" means "a break". To say you stop for a break, use "at holde" (to hold): "Vi holder pause klokken tolv" (We take a break at twelve). In music or speech, it also means "a pause". For example, "Der er en lang pause i musikken" (There is a long pause in the music).

sentence.da: Nu holder vi **pause** og drikker kaffe.
sentence.en: Now we take a break and drink coffee.

en pave.explanation: "En pave" means "a pope". To say where he lives, say: "Paven bor i Vatikanet" (The pope lives in the Vatican).

sentence.da: Katolikkerne har en **pave**, som bor i Rom.
sentence.en: Catholics have a pope, who lives in Rome.

en peberfrugt.explanation: "En peberfrugt" means "a bell pepper". It is built from "peber" (pepper) and "en frugt" (a fruit). The spice is just "peber" (pepper). For example, "Jeg strør peber på kødet" (I sprinkle pepper on the meat).

sentence.da: En rød **peberfrugt** smager sødt og er ikke stærk.
sentence.en: A red bell pepper tastes sweet and is not hot.

en peberkværn.explanation: "En peberkværn" means "a pepper mill". It is built from "peber" (pepper) and "en kværn" (a mill). To ask for it at the table, say: "Kan du række mig peberkværnen?" (Can you pass me the pepper mill?).

sentence.da: Hun maler frisk peber med en **peberkværn**.
sentence.en: She grinds fresh pepper with a pepper mill.

en pebernød.explanation: "En pebernød" means "a small Christmas spice cookie". It is built from "peber" (pepper) and "en nød" (a nut), but it has no nuts. In Denmark it is a traditional Christmas treat.

sentence.da: Til jul spiser jeg en **pebernød** eller to.
sentence.en: At Christmas I eat a spice cookie or two.

en pegefinger.explanation: "En pegefinger" means "an index finger". It is built from "at pege" (to point) and "en finger" (a finger). To say someone warns you, say: "Han løfter pegefingeren" (He raises his index finger).

sentence.da: Du bruger din **pegefinger**, når du peger på noget.
sentence.en: You use your index finger when you point at something.

en pels.explanation: "En pels" means "a fur". When you talk about the hair on an animal, it also means "fur": "Hundens pels er blød" (The dog's fur is soft). When you talk about a coat made of fur, say: "Hun har en pels på" (She is wearing a fur coat).

sentence.da: En **pels** er lavet af dyrehuder og holder dig varm.
sentence.en: A fur is made of animal skins and keeps you warm.

en pen.explanation: "En pen" means "a pen". Do not mix it up with "pæn" (nice, pretty), which is spelled with an æ. For example, "Det er en pæn kjole" (It is a pretty dress).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver mit navn med en **pen**.
sentence.en: I write my name with a pen.

en pendler.explanation: "En pendler" means "a commuter". It comes from the verb "at pendle" (to commute). To say you travel to work every day, say: "Jeg er pendler fra Roskilde" (I am a commuter from Roskilde).

sentence.da: Som **pendler** tager hun toget til arbejde hver dag.
sentence.en: As a commuter she takes the train to work every day.

en pengepung.explanation: "En pengepung" means "a purse", as in a small case for coins and bills. For the bag you carry on your shoulder, say "en håndtaske" (a handbag) instead: "Hun har sin telefon i håndtasken" (She has her phone in the handbag).

sentence.da: Jeg har kun en lille mønt i min **pengepung**.
sentence.en: I only have a small coin in my purse.

en pensel.explanation: "En pensel" means "a paintbrush". To say a brush for cleaning, use "en børste" (a brush) instead, as in "en tandbørste" (a toothbrush): "Jeg køber en ny tandbørste" (I am buying a new toothbrush).

sentence.da: Hun maler et billede med en tynd **pensel**.
sentence.en: She paints a picture with a thin paintbrush.

en pension.explanation: "En pension" means "a pension". When you say someone stops working because of age, use "at gå på pension" (to retire): "Min far går på pension i år" (My father retires this year).

sentence.da: Efter mange år på arbejde får hun nu en **pension**.
sentence.en: After many years at work, she now gets a pension.

en pensionist.explanation: "En pensionist" means "a retiree". It is built from "pension" (pension) and the ending "-ist", which names a person, as in "en turist" (a tourist). To say you are retired, say: "Jeg er pensionist" (I am a retiree).

sentence.da: Min nabo er **pensionist** og arbejder ikke mere.
sentence.en: My neighbor is a retiree and doesn't work anymore.

en periode.explanation: "En periode" means "a period" of time. To say you did something for a while without naming how long, say "i en periode" (for a period): "Jeg boede i Odense i en periode" (I lived in Odense for a while). To end a sentence, use "et punktum" (a period) instead: "Sæt et punktum efter sætningen" (Put a period after the sentence).

sentence.da: Jeg har haft en travl **periode** på arbejdet.
sentence.en: I have had a busy period at work.

en perron.explanation: "En perron" means "a platform", as in a train station. To say where you stand, say "på perronen" (on the platform): "Vi står på perronen" (We are standing on the platform).

sentence.da: Vi venter på toget på **perron** to.
sentence.en: We wait for the train on platform two.

en persienne.explanation: "En persienne" means "a blind", as in a window covering. To keep the sun out, say: "Jeg lukker persiennen" (I am closing the blind).

sentence.da: Soveværelset har en **persienne** mod solen.
sentence.en: The bedroom has a blind against the sun.

en person.explanation: "En person" means "a person". When you book a table, say: "Et bord til to personer" (A table for two people).

sentence.da: Billetten gælder for én **person**.
sentence.en: The ticket is valid for one person.

en personlig træner.explanation: "En personlig træner" means "a personal trainer". It is built from "personlig" (personal) and "en træner" (a trainer). To say the leader of a team, use "en træner" (a coach) alone: "Træneren har tyve spillere" (The coach has twenty players).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **personlig træner**, som laver mit træningsprogram.
sentence.en: I have a personal trainer who makes my training program.

en personlighed.explanation: "En personlighed" means "a personality". The ending "-hed" works like English "-ness", as in "en frihed" (a freedom). When you mean a famous person, it also means "a figure": "en kendt personlighed" (a well-known figure).

sentence.da: Humor er en vigtig del af hans **personlighed**.
sentence.en: Humor is an important part of his personality.

en pest.explanation: "En pest" means "a plague". To say you avoid someone completely, say: "Jeg undgår ham som pesten" (I avoid him like the plague).

sentence.da: En **pest** er en meget farlig sygdom, som smitter hurtigt.
sentence.en: A plague is a very dangerous disease that spreads quickly.

en ph.d..explanation: "En ph.d." means "a PhD". English writes "PhD", but Danish writes "ph.d." with dots. In Denmark a PhD student is employed by the university and gets a salary.

sentence.da: Hun er i gang med en **ph.d.** om børns sprog.
sentence.en: She is working on a PhD about children's language.

en picnic.explanation: "En picnic" means "a picnic". To suggest one, use "at tage på picnic" (to go on a picnic): "Skal vi tage på picnic i morgen?" (Shall we go on a picnic tomorrow?).

sentence.da: Vi tager på **picnic** i parken, når det er varmt.
sentence.en: We go on a picnic in the park when it is warm.

en pige.explanation: "En pige" means "a girl". For a grown woman, say "en kvinde" (a woman) instead: "Hun er en voksen kvinde" (She is a grown woman).

sentence.da: En **pige** og en dreng leger i haven.
sentence.en: A girl and a boy play in the garden.

en pil.explanation: "En pil" means "an arrow". It also means "a willow". For example, "Der står en pil i haven" (There is a willow in the garden). To say the tree by its full name, use "et piletræ" (a willow tree).

sentence.da: Skiltet har en **pil**, der peger til højre.
sentence.en: The sign has an arrow that points to the right.

en pille.explanation: "En pille" means "a pill". The form "pillen" (the pill) can mean the birth control pill. For example, "Hun tager pillen" (She takes the birth control pill).

sentence.da: Jeg har ondt og tager en **pille**.
sentence.en: I am in pain and take a pill.

en pilot.explanation: "En pilot" means "a pilot". To say what a pilot does, say: "Piloten lander flyet i København" (The pilot lands the plane in Copenhagen).

sentence.da: Min onkel er **pilot** og flyver til Asien.
sentence.en: My uncle is a pilot and flies to Asia.

en pind.explanation: "En pind" means "a stick". It is part of "spisepinde" (chopsticks), built from "at spise" (to eat) and "pinde" (sticks).

sentence.da: Hunden løber efter en **pind**.
sentence.en: The dog runs after a stick.

en pingvin.explanation: "En pingvin" means "a penguin". To name one kind of penguin, say "en kejserpingvin" (an emperor penguin): "Kejserpingvinen bor i Antarktis" (The emperor penguin lives in Antarctica).

sentence.da: En **pingvin** er en fugl, der svømmer.
sentence.en: A penguin is a bird that swims.

en pinkode.explanation: "En pinkode" means "a PIN code". It is built from "pin" (PIN) and "en kode" (a code).

sentence.da: Tast din **pinkode** ved kassen.
sentence.en: Enter your PIN code at the checkout.

en pirat.explanation: "En pirat" means "a pirate". Illegal copying of films and music is called "piratkopiering" (pirate copying), built from "pirat" and "at kopiere" (to copy).

sentence.da: Den onde **pirat** sejler over havet.
sentence.en: The evil pirate sails across the sea.

en pistol.explanation: "En pistol" means "a pistol". To talk about a long gun, use "et gevær" (a rifle): "Jægeren har et gevær" (The hunter has a rifle).

sentence.da: Han havde en **pistol** i lommen.
sentence.en: He had a pistol in his pocket.

en pita.explanation: "En pita" means "a pita". To name the filling, use "med" (with): "en pita med kebab" (a pita with kebab).

sentence.da: Jeg fylder en **pita** med salat og kylling.
sentence.en: I fill a pita with salad and chicken.

en pizza.explanation: "En pizza" means "a pizza". To order a pizza, use "at bestille" (to order): "Jeg vil gerne bestille en pizza" (I would like to order a pizza).

sentence.da: En **pizza** har bund, sauce og ost.
sentence.en: A pizza has a base, sauce and cheese.

et pizzeria.explanation: "Et pizzeria" means "a pizzeria". It is built from "pizza" and the ending "-eria".

sentence.da: Vi spiser pizza på et lille **pizzeria**.
sentence.en: We eat pizza at a small pizzeria.

en plade.explanation: "En plade" means "a plate or record". When you talk about music, it means a vinyl record: "Jeg køber en gammel plade" (I buy an old record). When you talk about a flat piece of material, it means a sheet: "en plade af træ" (a sheet of wood). For a plate you eat from, use "en tallerken" (a plate): "Maden ligger på en tallerken" (The food is on a plate).

sentence.da: Han lytter til en gammel **plade**.
sentence.en: He listens to an old record.

en pladespiller.explanation: "En pladespiller" means "a record player". It is built from "en plade" (a record) and "at spille" (to play).

sentence.da: På en **pladespiller** kan man høre musik fra sorte vinylplader.
sentence.en: On a record player you can hear music from black vinyl records.

en plads.explanation: "En plads" means "a seat or room or square". When you talk about where you sit on a train or in a cinema, it means "a seat": "Er denne plads optaget?" (Is this seat taken?). When you ask whether there is space, it means "room": "Er der plads?" (Is there room?). When you talk about a town square, it means "a square": "Vi mødes på pladsen" (We meet in the square).

forms.en: the seat / the room / the square

sentence.da: Der er ikke **plads** i bussen.
sentence.en: There is no room on the bus.

en plaid.explanation: "En plaid" means "a throw blanket". English speakers know "plaid" as a checked pattern, but in Danish it is a blanket. For the cover you sleep under at night, use "en dyne" (a duvet): "Jeg sover under en dyne" (I sleep under a duvet).

sentence.da: Jeg sidder i sofaen med en varm **plaid**.
sentence.en: I sit on the sofa with a warm throw blanket.

en plakat.explanation: "En plakat" means "a poster". A poster for a film is "en filmplakat" (a movie poster). For example, "Jeg har en filmplakat på væggen" (I have a movie poster on the wall).

sentence.da: Jeg har hængt en **plakat** op i mit værelse.
sentence.en: I have hung a poster up in my room.

en plan.explanation: "En plan" means "a plan". To ask what someone is doing, say: "Har du planer i weekenden?" (Do you have plans this weekend?). The word is also part of "en køreplan" (a timetable) and "en madplan" (a meal plan).

sentence.da: Vores **plan** er at tage toget.
sentence.en: Our plan is to take the train.

en planet.explanation: "En planet" means "a planet". To talk about the whole Earth as our home, use it too: "Vi skal passe på planeten" (We must take care of the planet).

sentence.da: Mars er en rød **planet**.
sentence.en: Mars is a red planet.

en planke.explanation: "En planke" means "a plank". To talk about a plank in a floor, use "en gulvplanke" (a floor plank): "Gulvplanken knirker" (The floor plank creaks).

sentence.da: Hvert stykke i gulvet er en **planke**.
sentence.en: Each piece in the floor is a plank.

en plante.explanation: "En plante" means "a plant". To say you put a tree in the ground, use the verb "at plante" (to plant): "Vi planter et træ" (We plant a tree).

sentence.da: Min **plante** har brug for mere lys.
sentence.en: My plant needs more light.

en planteskole.explanation: "En planteskole" means "a plant nursery". It is built from "en plante" (a plant) and "en skole" (a school). Do not mix it up with "en vuggestue" (a daycare for babies). For example, "Min søn går i vuggestue" (My son goes to daycare).

sentence.da: På en **planteskole** kan man købe unge træer og buske til haven.
sentence.en: At a plant nursery you can buy young trees and bushes for the garden.

en plastikpose.explanation: "En plastikpose" means "a plastic bag". It is built from "plastik" (plastic) and "en pose" (a bag). To ask a customer if they want a bag, say: "Vil du have en pose?" (Do you want a bag?).

sentence.da: Jeg har æbler i en **plastikpose**.
sentence.en: I have apples in a plastic bag.

en platform.explanation: "En platform" means "a platform", as in an online service. For the place where you wait for a train, use "en perron" (a station platform): "Toget kører fra perron tre" (The train leaves from platform three).

sentence.da: Instagram er en **platform**, hvor man deler billeder med venner.
sentence.en: Instagram is a platform where you share pictures with friends.

en playliste.explanation: "En playliste" means "a playlist". To say you put songs together, use "at lave" (to make): "Jeg laver en playliste til festen" (I make a playlist for the party).

sentence.da: Jeg lytter til min **playliste**, når jeg løber.
sentence.en: I listen to my playlist when I run.

en plejefamilie.explanation: "En plejefamilie" means "a foster family". It is built from "pleje" (care) and "en familie" (a family). In Denmark the municipality ("kommunen") decides when a child is placed in one.

sentence.da: Barnet bor hos en **plejefamilie**, fordi forældrene ikke kan tage sig af det.
sentence.en: The child lives with a foster family because the parents cannot take care of it.

en plet.explanation: "En plet" means "a stain". To describe a small area, it also means "a spot": "en grøn plet" (a green spot).

sentence.da: Der er en **plet** på min nye skjorte.
sentence.en: There is a stain on my new shirt.

en pligt.explanation: "En pligt" means "a duty". To say work comes before fun, use the saying "Pligt før fornøjelse" (Duty before pleasure).

sentence.da: Det er hans **pligt** at passe på børnene.
sentence.en: It is his duty to take care of the children.

en pligtfølelse.explanation: "En pligtfølelse" means "a sense of duty". It is built from "en pligt" (a duty) and "en følelse" (a feeling).

sentence.da: Af **pligtfølelse** passede hun sin syge mor hver dag.
sentence.en: Out of a sense of duty, she looked after her sick mother every day.

en plov.explanation: "En plov" means "a plow". To say you work the soil with it, use the verb "at pløje" (to plow): "Bonden pløjer marken" (The farmer plows the field).

sentence.da: Landmanden bruger en **plov** til at vende jorden.
sentence.en: The farmer uses a plow to turn the soil.

en plæne.explanation: "En plæne" means "a lawn". To say you mow a lawn, use "at klippe" (to cut): "Vi klipper plænen" (We mow the lawn). Do not mix it up with "græs" (grass). For example, "Græsset er vådt" (The grass is wet).

sentence.da: Vi spiser frokost på en grøn **plæne**.
sentence.en: We eat lunch on a green lawn.

en podcast.explanation: "En podcast" means "a podcast". To suggest listening to a podcast, use "at lytte til" (to listen to): "Skal vi lytte til en podcast?" (Shall we listen to a podcast?).

sentence.da: Jeg hører en **podcast**, når jeg cykler på arbejde.
sentence.en: I listen to a podcast when I bike to work.

en pointe.explanation: "En pointe" means "a point", as in the main idea of a story. For a score in a game, use "et point" (a point): "Holdet fik et point" (The team got one point).

sentence.da: Jeg forstod ikke hans **pointe**, før han forklarede det.
sentence.en: I did not understand his point until he explained it.

en pokal.explanation: "En pokal" means "a trophy". To say you won a trophy, use "at vinde" (to win): "Vi vandt pokalen" (We won the trophy).

sentence.da: Holdet fik en stor **pokal**, fordi det vandt finalen.
sentence.en: The team got a big trophy because it won the final.

en polak.explanation: "En polak" means "a Pole". To describe something from Poland, use "polsk" (Polish): "polsk pølse" (Polish sausage).

sentence.da: En **polak** kommer fra Polen.
sentence.en: A Pole comes from Poland.

en politibetjent.explanation: "En politibetjent" means "a police officer". It is built from "politi" (police) and "en betjent" (an officer). To say what someone's job is, leave out the article: "Hun er politibetjent" (She is a police officer).

sentence.da: Du kan bede en **politibetjent** om hjælp.
sentence.en: You can ask a police officer for help.

en politik.explanation: "En politik" means "a policy". When you talk about politics in general, leave out "en": "Han taler om politik" (He talks about politics).

sentence.da: Skolen har en klar **politik** mod mobning.
sentence.en: The school has a clear policy against bullying.

en politiker.explanation: "En politiker" means "a politician". It comes from "politik" (politics). To say who you vote for, use "at stemme på" (to vote for): "Jeg stemmer på en lokal politiker" (I vote for a local politician).

sentence.da: En **politiker** stemmer om love i Folketinget.
sentence.en: A politician votes on laws in the Parliament.

en politimand.explanation: "En politimand" means "a policeman". For a word that fits both men and women, use "en politibetjent" (a police officer): "Hun er politibetjent" (She is a police officer).

sentence.da: Jeg spurgte en **politimand** om vej.
sentence.en: I asked a policeman for directions.

en politistation.explanation: "En politistation" means "a police station". To say you are there, use "på" (at): "Jeg er på politistationen" (I am at the police station).

sentence.da: Politibetjenten arbejder på en **politistation**.
sentence.en: The police officer works at a police station.

en pollenallergi.explanation: "En pollenallergi" means "a pollen allergy". It is built from "pollen" (pollen) and "en allergi" (an allergy). To say you have it, use "at have" (to have) without an article: "Jeg har pollenallergi" (I have a pollen allergy).

sentence.da: Med **pollenallergi** er det svært at være ude, når birken blomstrer.
sentence.en: With a pollen allergy it is hard to be outside when the birch tree blooms.

en polo.explanation: "En polo" means "a polo shirt". A different use of the word is the sport, without an article: "Han spiller polo" (He plays polo).

sentence.da: Han har en hvid **polo** på til festen.
sentence.en: He is wearing a white polo shirt to the party.

en polterabend.explanation: "En polterabend" means "a pre-wedding party". The word comes from German, where "poltern" means to make a loud banging noise.

sentence.da: Aftenen før brylluppet holder vennerne en **polterabend** for brudeparret.
sentence.en: The evening before the wedding, the friends hold a pre-wedding party for the bridal couple.

en pony.explanation: "En pony" means "a pony". Do not mix it up with "en hest" (a horse). For example, "Hesten løber hurtigt" (The horse runs fast).

sentence.da: Min datter rider på en **pony** hver lørdag.
sentence.en: My daughter rides a pony every Saturday.

en pool.explanation: "En pool" means "a pool", as in a swimming pool. For a big public pool building, use "en svømmehal" (a swimming hall): "Vi svømmer i svømmehallen" (We swim in the swimming hall).

sentence.da: Vi har en lille **pool** i haven.
sentence.en: We have a small pool in the garden.

en porre.explanation: "En porre" means "a leek". A soup made with leeks is "porresuppe" (leek soup). For example, "Vi spiser porresuppe" (We eat leek soup).

sentence.da: Jeg laver suppe med **porre** og kartofler.
sentence.en: I make soup with leek and potatoes.

en port.explanation: "En port" means "a gate". For a small gate in a garden, use "en låge" (a small gate): "Haven har en låge" (The garden has a small gate). The door of a garage is "en garageport" (a garage door).

sentence.da: Gården har en stor **port** til bilerne.
sentence.en: The yard has a big gate for the cars.

en portion.explanation: "En portion" means "a portion". To order food by the portion, put the food after it: "Jeg vil gerne have en portion pommes frites" (I would like a portion of fries).

sentence.da: Én **portion** er nok til en person.
sentence.en: One portion is enough for one person.

en pose.explanation: "En pose" means "a bag". To name what is inside, put the food after it: "en pose chips" (a bag of chips). For a bag you carry on your shoulder, use "en taske" (a bag, purse): "Hun har en taske på skulderen" (She has a bag on her shoulder).

sentence.da: Jeg lagde æblerne i en **pose** af papir.
sentence.en: I put the apples in a paper bag.

en position.explanation: "En position" means "a position", as in a place on a team. To talk about a job at the top of a company, say: "en ledende position" (a leading position).

sentence.da: Hvilken **position** spiller du på holdet?
sentence.en: Which position do you play on the team?

en postkasse.explanation: "En postkasse" means "a mailbox". It is built from "post" (mail) and "en kasse" (a box). In a shop, "kassen" (the checkout) uses the same word. For example, "Jeg betaler ved kassen" (I pay at the checkout).

sentence.da: Postbuddet lægger breve i vores **postkasse**.
sentence.en: The mail carrier puts letters in our mailbox.

en pote.explanation: "En pote" means "a paw". To tell a dog to shake hands, say: "Giv pote!" (Shake!).

sentence.da: Hunden har ondt i en **pote** og halter.
sentence.en: The dog has a sore paw and limps.

en potte.explanation: "En potte" means "a pot", as in a pot for a plant. A different use is the potty for a small child: "Han sidder på potten" (He sits on the potty).

sentence.da: Jeg har sat basilikum i en **potte** på vindueskarmen.
sentence.en: I have put basil in a pot on the windowsill.

en potteplante.explanation: "En potteplante" means "a houseplant". It is built from "en potte" (a pot) and "en plante" (a plant).

sentence.da: Min **potteplante** står i en potte og skal have vand.
sentence.en: My houseplant stands in a pot and needs water.

en praksis.explanation: "En praksis" means "a practice", as in how something is really done. To say how it works in real life, use "i praksis" (in practice): "I praksis er det svært" (In practice it is hard). A doctor's office is "en lægepraksis" (a doctor's practice). For example, "Hun arbejder i en lægepraksis" (She works in a doctor's practice).

sentence.da: Jeg har lært teorien, men jeg mangler **praksis**.
sentence.en: I have learned the theory, but I lack practice.

en praktikant.explanation: "En praktikant" means "an intern". A period of work like this is called "praktik" (work placement). For example, "Jeg er i praktik" (I am on a work placement).

sentence.da: Som **praktikant** lærer man jobbet ved at hjælpe de andre.
sentence.en: As an intern you learn the job by helping the others.

en praktikplads.explanation: "En praktikplads" means "an internship placement". It is built from "praktik" (work placement) and "en plads" (a place). In Denmark, students in vocational programs must find one at a company to complete their education.

sentence.da: Jeg skal have en **praktikplads**, før jeg kan blive færdig med uddannelsen.
sentence.en: I need an internship placement before I can finish my education.

en praktiserende læge.explanation: "En praktiserende læge" means "a general practitioner". It is built from "praktiserende" (practicing) and "en læge" (a doctor). To say you are going to see the doctor, use "at gå til" (to go to): "Jeg skal til lægen i morgen" (I am going to the doctor tomorrow).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til min **praktiserende læge**, hvis jeg bliver syg.
sentence.en: I call my general practitioner if I get sick.

en premiere.explanation: "En premiere" means "a premiere". To say a film opens, use "at have premiere" (to have a premiere): "Filmen har premiere i morgen" (The film opens tomorrow).

sentence.da: I aften er der **premiere** på det nye teaterstykke.
sentence.en: Tonight there is a premiere of the new play.

en presse.explanation: "En presse" means "a press", as in the news media. For example, "Pressen skriver om det" (The press is writing about it). A different meaning is a machine that squeezes things. For another example, "en saftpresse" (a juicer).

sentence.da: Der var meget **presse** til stede, da ministeren kom.
sentence.en: There was a lot of press present when the minister arrived.

en prik.explanation: "En prik" means "a dot". The word for dotted is "prikket". For example, "en prikket kjole" (a dotted dress).

sentence.da: Tegn en **prik** med pennen, ikke en streg.
sentence.en: Draw a dot with the pen, not a line.

en prins.explanation: "En prins" means "a prince". When you use it as a title with a name, put it first: "Prins Henrik var gift med dronning Margrethe" (Prince Henrik was married to Queen Margrethe).

sentence.da: En **prins** er søn af en konge.
sentence.en: A prince is the son of a king.

en prinsesse.explanation: "En prinsesse" means "a princess". It is the female form of "en prins" (a prince).

sentence.da: Hun har en krone på og ligner en **prinsesse**.
sentence.en: She has a crown on and looks like a princess.

en printer.explanation: "En printer" means "a printer". To print a document, use the verb "at printe" (to print): "Jeg printer dokumentet" (I print the document).

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge en **printer** til at printe dokumentet.
sentence.en: I need a printer to print the document.

en prioritering.explanation: "En prioritering" means "a prioritization". It comes from the verb "at prioritere" (to prioritize). To say you must choose what to do first, say: "Vi må lave en prioritering" (We have to make a prioritization).

sentence.da: Med så få penge er en klar **prioritering** nødvendig.
sentence.en: With so little money, a clear prioritization is necessary.

en prioritet.explanation: "En prioritet" means "a priority". It is built on the verb "at prioritere" (to prioritize). To say something matters a lot, use "høj prioritet" (high priority): "Sikkerhed er en høj prioritet her" (Safety is a high priority here).

sentence.da: Min families trivsel er min højeste **prioritet** lige nu.
sentence.en: My family's well-being is my highest priority right now.

en pris.explanation: "En pris" means "a price". To say what something costs, use "på" (of): "en pris på tyve kroner" (a price of twenty crowns). It also means "a prize" or "an award". To say you win one, use "at vinde" (to win): "Hun vandt en pris" (She won a prize).

sentence.da: Den lave **pris** gør varen billig.
sentence.en: The low price makes the item cheap.

en prisforskel.explanation: "En prisforskel" means "a price difference". It is built from "en pris" (a price) and "en forskel" (a difference). "Forskel" is also in the phrase "Det gør ingen forskel" (It makes no difference).

sentence.da: Der er en stor **prisforskel** mellem butikkerne.
sentence.en: There is a big price difference between the stores.

en prisstigning.explanation: "En prisstigning" means "a price increase". It is built from "en pris" (a price) and "en stigning" (a rise). The verb in it is "at stige" (to rise). For example, "Priserne stiger" (Prices are rising).

sentence.da: Der kommer en **prisstigning** på mælk fra næste måned.
sentence.en: There is a price increase on milk from next month.

en privatperson.explanation: "En privatperson" means "a private individual". It is built from "privat" (private) and "en person" (a person). To say an offer is not for companies, use the plural: "Tilbuddet er kun for privatpersoner" (The offer is only for private individuals).

sentence.da: Banken har andre regler for en **privatperson** end for et firma.
sentence.en: The bank has other rules for a private individual than for a firm.

en problemstilling.explanation: "En problemstilling" means "an issue". The first part is "et problem" (a problem). To say a text looks at an issue closely, use "at belyse" (to shed light on): "Rapporten belyser en vigtig problemstilling" (The report sheds light on an important issue).

sentence.da: I opgaven undersøger vi en **problemstilling** om unges søvn.
sentence.en: In the assignment, we investigate an issue about young people's sleep.

en procedure.explanation: "En procedure" means "a procedure". To say you follow the steps, use "at følge" (to follow): "Vi følger en procedure" (We follow a procedure). Do not mix it up with "en proces" (a process). For example, "Det er en lang proces" (It is a long process).

sentence.da: Der er en fast **procedure** for nye kunder.
sentence.en: There is a set procedure for new customers.

en procent.explanation: "En procent" means "a percent". When you say a number before it, "procent" stays the same: "tre procent" (three percent). To say you are completely sure, say: "Jeg er hundrede procent sikker" (I am one hundred percent sure).

sentence.da: Kun fem **procent** af eleverne er syge.
sentence.en: Only five percent of the students are sick.

en proces.explanation: "En proces" means "a process". To say you start one, use "at sætte i gang" (to start): "Vi sætter en proces i gang" (We start a process). Do not mix it up with "en procedure" (a procedure). For example, "Vi følger en procedure" (We follow a procedure).

sentence.da: At lære et sprog er en langsom **proces**.
sentence.en: Learning a language is a slow process.

en producer.explanation: "En producer" means "a producer", as in film, TV or music. For a company that makes goods, use "en producent" (a manufacturer): "Producenten sælger varer til butikkerne" (The manufacturer sells goods to the shops).

sentence.da: Min ven er **producer** og laver film.
sentence.en: My friend is a producer and makes films.

en professor.explanation: "En professor" means "a professor". For a teacher at a normal school, use "en lærer" (a teacher): "Min lærer hedder Anna" (My teacher is called Anna).

sentence.da: En **professor** underviser på et universitet.
sentence.en: A professor teaches at a university.

en profil.explanation: "En profil" means "a profile", as in your page on a website or app. To describe a side view of a face, use "i profil" (in profile): "Fotoet viser hende i profil" (The photo shows her in profile).

sentence.da: Jeg har skrevet lidt om mig selv på min **profil**.
sentence.en: I wrote a little about myself on my profile.

en programmør.explanation: "En programmør" means "a programmer". It comes from "et program" (a program). To say what someone's job is, leave out the article: "Hun er programmør" (She is a programmer).

sentence.da: En **programmør** skriver kode til computere.
sentence.en: A programmer writes code for computers.

en projektleder.explanation: "En projektleder" means "a project manager". It is built from "et projekt" (a project) and "en leder" (a leader). The ending "-leder" is also in "en afdelingsleder" (a department manager).

sentence.da: Hun er **projektleder** og sørger for, at alle når deres frister.
sentence.en: She is a project manager and makes sure everyone meets their deadlines.

en proptrækker.explanation: "En proptrækker" means "a corkscrew". It is built from "en prop" (a cork) and "at trække" (to pull). A different use of "prop" is a blockage: "Der er en trafikprop" (There is a traffic jam).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke åbne vinen uden en **proptrækker**.
sentence.en: I cannot open the wine without a corkscrew.

en protest.explanation: "En protest" means "a protest". The verb is "at protestere" (to protest). For example, "Eleverne protesterer mod reglen" (The students protest against the rule).

sentence.da: Mange gik på gaden i **protest** mod de nye regler.
sentence.en: Many went into the street in protest against the new rules.

en præmie.explanation: "En præmie" means "a prize". For the amount you pay for insurance, it means "a premium": "Præmien er tusind kroner om året" (The premium is a thousand kroner a year).

sentence.da: Vinderen af konkurrencen får en stor **præmie**.
sentence.en: The winner of the contest gets a big prize.

en præsentation.explanation: "En præsentation" means "a presentation". It comes from the verb "at præsentere" (to present). To say you prepare one, use "at lave" (to make): "Jeg laver en præsentation til kunden" (I make a presentation for the customer).

sentence.da: Jeg skal holde en **præsentation** på mandag.
sentence.en: I am going to give a presentation on Monday.

en præsident.explanation: "En præsident" means "a president". Denmark has no president, because its head of state is the king.

sentence.da: En **præsident** leder et land.
sentence.en: A president leads a country.

en præst.explanation: "En præst" means "a priest". In Denmark it is also the word for a minister in the Church of Denmark. To say what someone's job is, leave out the article: "Hun er præst i Roskilde" (She is a priest in Roskilde).

sentence.da: Vores **præst** holder en tale i kirken.
sentence.en: Our priest gives a speech in church.

en præstation.explanation: "En præstation" means "a performance", as in how well someone does. For a show on a stage, use "en forestilling" (a show): "Vi ser en forestilling i teatret" (We see a show at the theater).

sentence.da: Han leverede en flot **præstation** og vandt løbet.
sentence.en: He delivered a fine performance and won the race.

en prøve.explanation: "En prøve" means "a test or a sample". When you talk about school, it means "a test": "Vi har en prøve i matematik" (We have a test in math). When you talk about a small bit to try, it means "a sample": "en prøve af osten" (a sample of the cheese).

sentence.da: Vi skriver en **prøve** i geografi på fredag.
sentence.en: We are taking a test in geography on Friday.

en prøvetid.explanation: "En prøvetid" means "a probation period". It is built from "en prøve" (a test) and "en tid" (a time). To say you are still in it, use "at være i" (to be in): "Jeg er stadig i prøvetid" (I am still on probation).

sentence.da: En ny medarbejder har en **prøvetid** på tre måneder.
sentence.en: A new employee has a probation period of three months.

en psykiater.explanation: "En psykiater" means "a psychiatrist". To say you are going to see one, say: "Jeg skal til psykiater" (I am going to see a psychiatrist). Do not mix it up with "en psykolog" (a psychologist), who is not a medical doctor. For example, "Jeg skal til psykolog" (I am going to see a psychologist).

sentence.da: En **psykiater** taler med patienter om deres tanker og følelser.
sentence.en: A psychiatrist talks with patients about their thoughts and feelings.

en psykolog.explanation: "En psykolog" means "a psychologist". To say you are going to see one, say: "Jeg skal til psykolog" (I am going to see a psychologist). Do not mix it up with "en psykiater" (a psychiatrist), who is a medical doctor. For example, "Jeg skal til psykiater" (I am going to see a psychiatrist).

sentence.da: Hun taler med en **psykolog** om sine bekymringer.
sentence.en: She talks to a psychologist about her worries.

en psykopat.explanation: "En psykopat" means "a psychopath". It is also used as a harsh word for someone who behaves wildly: "Han kørte som en psykopat" (He drove like a maniac).

sentence.da: Krimien handler om en **psykopat**, som dræber uden at fortryde det.
sentence.en: The crime novel is about a psychopath who kills without regret.

en publikation.explanation: "En publikation" means "a publication". Do not mix it up with "publikum" (audience). For example, "Publikum klappede" (The audience clapped), but "Forskeren læser en publikation" (The researcher reads a publication).

sentence.da: Forskerne udgav en **publikation** om børns søvn.
sentence.en: The researchers released a publication about children's sleep.

en pude.explanation: "En pude" means "a pillow". To talk about a soft cushion for a sofa, it means "a cushion": "Der ligger en pude i sofaen" (There is a cushion on the sofa). A pillow for your head is also "en hovedpude" (literally, a head pillow).

sentence.da: Mit hoved ligger på en blød **pude**.
sentence.en: My head lies on a soft pillow.

en puls.explanation: "En puls" means "a pulse". To say someone checks it, use "at måle" (to measure): "Lægen måler min puls" (The doctor measures my pulse).

sentence.da: Efter løbeturen er min **puls** høj, og jeg er forpustet.
sentence.en: After the run my pulse is high and I am out of breath.

en pung.explanation: "En pung" means "a wallet". To say you have to pay a lot, use the phrase "at punge ud" (to pay up): "Vi måtte punge ud for en ny bil" (We had to pay up for a new car).

sentence.da: Mine penge er i min **pung**.
sentence.en: My money is in my wallet.

en punktering.explanation: "En punktering" means "a flat tire or a puncture". To say a tire gets a hole, use the verb "at punktere" (to puncture): "Min cykel punkterede" (My bike got a flat tire).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke cykle, fordi jeg har en **punktering**.
sentence.en: I can't bike because I have a flat tire.

en pyjamas.explanation: "En pyjamas" means "a pair of pajamas". Danish counts it as one thing, so it takes "en". For example, "Jeg har fået en ny pyjamas" (I got a new pair of pajamas). English speakers spell "pajamas" with "a", but the Danish word is spelled with "y".

sentence.da: Jeg har min **pyjamas** på i sengen.
sentence.en: I am wearing my pajamas in bed.

en pyt.explanation: "En pyt" means "a puddle". To say "never mind", use the word "Pyt!" without "en": "Pyt, det gør ikke noget" (Never mind, it does not matter).

sentence.da: Der er en stor **pyt** midt på vejen.
sentence.en: There is a big puddle in the middle of the road.

en påskeferie.explanation: "En påskeferie" means "an Easter vacation". It is built from "påske" (Easter) and "en ferie" (a vacation). To wish someone a happy holiday, say: "Glædelig påske!" (Happy Easter!).

sentence.da: Skolen holder lukket i en uges **påskeferie**.
sentence.en: The school is closed for a week of Easter vacation.

en påskefrokost.explanation: "En påskefrokost" means "an Easter lunch". It is built from "påske" (Easter) and "en frokost" (a lunch), like "en julefrokost" (a Christmas lunch). In Denmark, a special beer called "påskebryg" (Easter brew) is sold for this season.

sentence.da: Hele familien samles til en lang **påskefrokost** med sild og æg.
sentence.en: The whole family gathers for a long Easter lunch with herring and eggs.

en påstand.explanation: "En påstand" means "a claim". To say something has not been proven, say: "Det er kun en påstand" (It is only a claim).

sentence.da: Hun kan ikke bevise sin **påstand**, så ingen tror på den.
sentence.en: She cannot prove her claim, so nobody believes it.

en påvirkning.explanation: "En påvirkning" means "an influence". It comes from the verb "at påvirke" (to affect). For being drunk, it is used in "kørsel under påvirkning" (driving under the influence).

sentence.da: Skærme har en stor **påvirkning** af børns søvn.
sentence.en: Screens have a big influence on children's sleep.

en pædagog.explanation: "En pædagog" means "a daycare worker". In Denmark, "en pædagog" also works with children after school hours in "en SFO" (an after-school program).

sentence.da: En **pædagog** passer børn i en børnehave.
sentence.en: A daycare worker looks after children in a kindergarten.

en pære.explanation: "En pære" means "a pear". When you talk about a lamp, it also means "a light bulb": "en ny pære til lampen" (a new bulb for the lamp).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en sød **pære** og et æble.
sentence.en: I eat a sweet pear and an apple.

en pølse.explanation: "En pølse" means "a sausage". To order a hot dog, say: "Jeg vil gerne have en hotdog" (I would like a hot dog). A street stand that sells them is "en pølsevogn" (a hot dog stand).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en varm **pølse** med brød.
sentence.en: I eat a hot sausage with bread.

en pølsevogn.explanation: "En pølsevogn" means "a hot dog stand". It is built from "en pølse" (a sausage) and "en vogn" (a wagon). "Vogn" is also in "en indkøbsvogn" (a shopping cart) and "en barnevogn" (a stroller).

sentence.da: Hun sælger varme pølser fra en **pølsevogn**.
sentence.en: She sells hot dogs from a hot dog stand.

et palads.explanation: "Et palads" means "a palace". To talk about a palace in a story, say: "Prinsessen bor i et palads" (The princess lives in a palace). Do not mix it up with "et slot" (a castle).

sentence.da: Et **palads** har mange store sale og en stor have.
sentence.en: A palace has many big halls and a big garden.

et par.explanation: "Et par" means "a couple or a pair". To talk about two things that belong together, say: "et par sko" (a pair of shoes). To say a small number, put it before a noun: "et par dage" (a couple of days). To talk about two people in a relationship, say: "De er et sødt par" (They are a sweet couple).

sentence.da: Jeg bliver her et **par** dage.
sentence.en: I will stay here for a couple of days.

et par jeans.explanation: "Et par jeans" means "a pair of jeans". To say what colour they are, put the colour after "et par": "et par sorte jeans" (a pair of black jeans). To say you are wearing jeans, leave out "et par": "Jeg har jeans på" (I am wearing jeans).

sentence.da: Jeg køber et **par jeans** i dag.
sentence.en: I am buying a pair of jeans today.

et paradis.explanation: "Et paradis" means "a paradise". To say a place is a paradise for a certain group, use "for": "et paradis for børn" (a paradise for children).

sentence.da: Øen er et **paradis** med hvide strande og blåt vand.
sentence.en: The island is a paradise with white beaches and blue water.

et paraplystativ.explanation: "Et paraplystativ" means "an umbrella stand". It is built from "en paraply" (an umbrella) and "et stativ" (a stand).

sentence.da: Jeg sætter den våde paraply i et **paraplystativ**.
sentence.en: I put the wet umbrella in an umbrella stand.

et parkeringshus.explanation: "Et parkeringshus" means "a parking garage". It is built from "en parkering" (parking) and "et hus" (a house).

sentence.da: Der er ingen pladser på gaden, men der er et **parkeringshus**.
sentence.en: There are no spaces on the street, but there is a parking garage.

et parti.explanation: "Et parti" means "a party", as in a political party. To talk about one game of chess, use it for a game: "Vi spiller et parti skak" (We are playing a game of chess). For a party with food and music, use "en fest" (a party): "Vi holder fest i morgen" (We are having a party tomorrow).

sentence.da: Socialdemokratiet er et stort **parti** i Danmark.
sentence.en: The Social Democrats are a big party in Denmark.

et pas.explanation: "Et pas" means "a passport". To ask to see one, say: "Må jeg se dit pas?" (May I see your passport?). Do not mix it up with "at passe" (to fit). For example, "Skoen passer" (The shoe fits).

sentence.da: Ved grænsen skal du vise dit **pas**.
sentence.en: At the border you must show your passport.

et pasfoto.explanation: "Et pasfoto" means "a passport photo". It is built from "et pas" (a passport) and "et foto" (a photo). "Foto" is also in "et fotoalbum" (a photo album).

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge et nyt **pasfoto** til mit pas.
sentence.en: I need a new passport photo for my passport.

et penalhus.explanation: "Et penalhus" means "a pencil case". It ends in "hus" (house), as in "et parkeringshus" (a parking garage).

sentence.da: Min kuglepen ligger i mit **penalhus**.
sentence.en: My pen is in my pencil case.

et pengeskab.explanation: "Et pengeskab" means "a safe". It is built from "penge" (money) and "et skab" (a cupboard). "Skab" is also in "et køleskab" (a refrigerator).

sentence.da: Vi gemmer vigtige papirer og smykker i et **pengeskab**.
sentence.en: We keep important papers and jewelry in a safe.

et pensum.explanation: "Et pensum" means "a syllabus". To say something is not part of the course material, use "ikke på pensum" (not on the syllabus): "Det kapitel er ikke på pensum" (That chapter is not on the syllabus).

sentence.da: Hele bogen er **pensum**, så vi skal læse den.
sentence.en: The whole book is on the syllabus, so we have to read it.

et personalemøde.explanation: "Et personalemøde" means "a staff meeting". It is built from "personale" (staff) and "et møde" (a meeting). "Møde" is also in "et forældremøde" (a parents' meeting).

sentence.da: Alle lærerne mødes til et **personalemøde** hver mandag.
sentence.en: All the teachers meet at a staff meeting every Monday.

et perspektiv.explanation: "Et perspektiv" means "a perspective". To say someone's view is interesting, say: "Det er et interessant perspektiv" (That is an interesting perspective). In drawing, it means making a flat picture look deep. For example, "Tegn huset i perspektiv" (Draw the house in perspective).

sentence.da: Børn og voksne har ikke det samme **perspektiv** på verden.
sentence.en: Children and adults do not have the same perspective on the world.

et pindsvin.explanation: "Et pindsvin" means "a hedgehog". Literally, it is a "stick hog".

sentence.da: Et **pindsvin** har pigge på ryggen og kan rulle sig sammen.
sentence.en: A hedgehog has spines on its back and can roll up into a ball.

et piskeris.explanation: "Et piskeris" means "a whisk". It is built from "at piske" (to whip) and "ris" (twigs).

sentence.da: Jeg rører æg og mel med et **piskeris**.
sentence.en: I mix eggs and flour with a whisk.

et plaster.explanation: "Et plaster" means "a band-aid". To talk about a pack of band-aids, use the plural form "plastre": "en pakke plastre" (a pack of band-aids).

sentence.da: Sæt et **plaster** på såret.
sentence.en: Put a band-aid on the wound.

et plejebarn.explanation: "Et plejebarn" means "a foster child". It is built from "pleje" (care) and "et barn" (a child). Do not mix it up with "et adoptivbarn" (an adopted child). For example, "De har et adoptivbarn fra Kina" (They have an adopted child from China).

sentence.da: Et **plejebarn** bor hos en anden familie, fordi forældrene ikke kan passe det.
sentence.en: A foster child lives with another family because the parents cannot take care of it.

et point.explanation: "Et point" means "a point", as in a game or test. To say how many you scored, say: "Hun fik ti point" (She got ten points). To make a point in an argument, use "en pointe": "Det var en god pointe" (That was a good point).

sentence.da: Vi mangler kun et **point** for at vinde.
sentence.en: We only need one more point to win.

et postbud.explanation: "Et postbud" means "a mail carrier". It is built from "post" (mail) and "et bud" (a messenger).

sentence.da: Et **postbud** står ved døren med en pakke.
sentence.en: A mail carrier is at the door with a package.

et posthus.explanation: "Et posthus" means "a post office". It is built from "post" (mail) and "et hus" (a house). To say you are going there, say: "Jeg skal på posthuset" (I am going to the post office).

sentence.da: Jeg skal sende en pakke fra et **posthus**.
sentence.en: I have to send a package from a post office.

et postkontor.explanation: "Et postkontor" means "a post office". It is built from "post" (mail) and "et kontor" (an office). To say you are going there, say: "Jeg skal på postkontoret" (I am going to the post office).

sentence.da: Jeg sender en pakke på et **postkontor**.
sentence.en: I send a package at a post office.

et postkort.explanation: "Et postkort" means "a postcard". It is built from "post" (mail) and "et kort" (a card). "Kort" is also in "et kreditkort" (a credit card).

sentence.da: På ferie sender jeg et **postkort** hjem.
sentence.en: On vacation, I send a postcard home.

et postnummer.explanation: "Et postnummer" means "a postal code". It is built from "post" (mail) and "et nummer" (a number). To write a Danish address, put the four-digit postal code before the town: "2100 København Ø" (2100 Copenhagen Ø).

sentence.da: Hvad er dit **postnummer**, så jeg kan sende pakken?
sentence.en: What is your postal code, so I can send the package?

et potentiale.explanation: "Et potentiale" means "a potential". To say something has potential in general, leave out "et": "Der er potentiale i idéen" (There is potential in the idea).

sentence.da: Den unge spiller har et stort **potentiale**, men skal træne mere.
sentence.en: The young player has great potential but needs to train more.

et princip.explanation: "Et princip" means "a principle". To say you do something because of your beliefs, use "af princip" (on principle): "Jeg spiser ikke kød af princip" (I do not eat meat on principle). To say something is true in theory, use "i princip" (in principle): "I princip kan alle komme" (In principle, anyone can come).

sentence.da: Det er et vigtigt **princip**, at alle får samme chance.
sentence.en: It is an important principle that everyone gets the same chance.

et prisfald.explanation: "Et prisfald" means "a price drop". It is built from "en pris" (a price) and "et fald" (a fall). "Fald" is also in "et snefald" (a snowfall).

sentence.da: Efter jul kommer der ofte et **prisfald**.
sentence.en: After Christmas there is often a price drop.

et prisskilt.explanation: "Et prisskilt" means "a price tag". It is built from "en pris" (a price) and "et skilt" (a sign). "Skilt" is also in "et gadeskilt" (a street sign).

sentence.da: Prisen står på et **prisskilt** ved jakken.
sentence.en: The price is on a price tag by the jacket.

et problem.explanation: "Et problem" means "a problem". To say "no problem" when someone thanks you or asks a favor, say: "Det er ikke noget problem" (It is no problem).

sentence.da: Vi har et **problem** med bilen.
sentence.en: We have a problem with the car.
