et produkt.explanation: "Et produkt" means "a product". To say where a product comes from, put the country adjective before it: "et dansk produkt" (a Danish product).

sentence.da: Vi sælger et nyt **produkt** i butikken.
sentence.en: We sell a new product in the shop.

et program.explanation: "Et program" means "a program", as on a computer. When you ask what is planned for the day, it means "schedule": "Hvad er programmet i dag?" (What is the plan today?)

sentence.da: Jeg skal installere et nyt **program** på min computer.
sentence.en: I have to install a new program on my computer.

et projekt.explanation: "Et projekt" means "a project". To say you are beginning one, say: "Vi starter et nyt projekt i dag" (We are starting a new project today).

sentence.da: Vi arbejder på et stort **projekt** sammen.
sentence.en: We are working on a big project together.

et prøverum.explanation: "Et prøverum" means "a fitting room". It is built from "at prøve" (to try) and "et rum" (a room).

sentence.da: Jeg prøver bukserne i et **prøverum**.
sentence.en: I try on the pants in a fitting room.

et pseudonym.explanation: "Et pseudonym" means "a pseudonym". To ask for an author's pen name, say: "Hvad er hendes pseudonym?" (What is her pseudonym?) Do not mix it up with "anonym" (anonymous), which means no name is given at all: "Brevet er anonymt" (The letter is anonymous).

sentence.da: Forfatteren skrev bøgerne under et **pseudonym**, så ingen kendte hendes rigtige navn.
sentence.en: The author wrote the books under a pseudonym, so no one knew her real name.

et pudebetræk.explanation: "Et pudebetræk" means "a pillowcase". It is built from "en pude" (a pillow) and "et betræk" (a cover). "Betræk" is also in "et sofabetræk" (a sofa cover).

sentence.da: Jeg putter puden i et **pudebetræk**.
sentence.en: I put the pillow in a pillowcase.

et pulver.explanation: "Et pulver" means "a powder". It is also the last part of "bagepulver" (baking powder).

sentence.da: Rør **pulver** ud i varmt vand.
sentence.en: Stir powder into hot water.

et pund.explanation: "Et pund" means "a pound", as in British money. When you buy food by weight, "et pund" is 500 grams: "Jeg køber et pund smør" (I am buying 500 grams of butter).

sentence.da: Billetten til London koster tyve **pund**.
sentence.en: The ticket to London costs twenty pounds.

et punkt.explanation: "Et punkt" means "a point or spot". To name a weak spot, say: "et svagt punkt" (a weak point). Do not mix it up with "et punktum" (a period). For example, "Sæt et punktum efter sætningen" (Put a period after the sentence).

sentence.da: Det første **punkt** på listen er mælk.
sentence.en: The first item on the list is milk.

et punktum.explanation: "Et punktum" means "a period", as in the punctuation mark. To say a matter is closed, say "Punktum!" (That's final!): "Jeg har sagt nej, punktum!" (I said no, period!)

sentence.da: Der skal være et **punktum** i slutningen af sætningen.
sentence.en: There has to be a period at the end of the sentence.

et puslespil.explanation: "Et puslespil" means "a puzzle". To say you are doing one, use "at lægge" (to put): "Vi lægger et puslespil" (We are doing a puzzle). Do not mix it up with "en gåde" (a riddle). For example, "Kan du løse den gåde?" (Can you solve that riddle?)

sentence.da: Et **puslespil** har mange små brikker.
sentence.en: A puzzle has many small pieces.

et påfund.explanation: "Et påfund" means "an idea or invention". It comes from "at finde på" (to think up). To ask what someone has come up with, say: "Hvad er det for et påfund?" (What kind of idea is that?)

sentence.da: Det er hans eget **påfund**, og ingen andre har prøvet det.
sentence.en: It is his own idea, and nobody else has tried it.

et påskeæg.explanation: "Et påskeæg" means "an Easter egg". It is built from "påske" (Easter) and "et æg" (an egg). In Denmark, someone who guesses who sent a "gækkebrev" (a teasing Easter letter) wins an Easter egg.

sentence.da: Til påske får jeg et **påskeæg** af chokolade.
sentence.en: At Easter I get an Easter egg made of chocolate.

pandehår.explanation: "Et pandehår" means "bangs". It is built from "en pande" (a forehead) and "et hår" (a hair). To say someone has bangs, leave out "et": "Hun har pandehår" (She has bangs).

sentence.da: Hendes **pandehår** hænger ned over panden og øjnene.
sentence.en: Her bangs hang down over her forehead and eyes.

panik.explanation: "Panik" means "panic". To say someone suddenly panicked, use "at gå i panik" (to panic): "Hun gik i panik" (She panicked).

sentence.da: Der opstod **panik**, da alarmen gik i gang.
sentence.en: Panic broke out when the alarm went off.

pant.explanation: "Pant" means "deposit". In Denmark, you get the "pant" back when you return an empty bottle or can to a shop.

forms.en: to return bottles for the deposit

sentence.da: Der er **pant** på flasken.
sentence.en: There is a deposit on the bottle.

pap.explanation: "Pap" means "cardboard". To say what something is cut from, say: "Han klipper en figur ud af pap" (He cuts a shape out of cardboard). Do not mix it up with "papir" (paper). For example, "Jeg skriver på papir" (I write on paper).

sentence.da: Kassen er lavet af tyk **pap** og er let.
sentence.en: The box is made of thick cardboard and is light.

papir.explanation: "Papir" means "a paper". To talk about the material, leave out "et": "Vi bruger ikke plastik, kun papir" (We do not use plastic, only paper). In the plural, "papirer" also means "documents". For example, "Har du dine papirer med?" (Do you have your papers with you?)

sentence.da: Jeg printer brevet på **papir**.
sentence.en: I print the letter on paper.

paradoksal.explanation: "Paradoksal" means "paradoxical". It comes from the noun "et paradoks" (a paradox).

sentence.da: Situationen er **paradoksal**: Jo mere han sparer, jo mere bruger han.
sentence.en: The situation is paradoxical: the more he saves, the more he spends.

paranoid.explanation: "Paranoid" means "paranoid". To tell someone they are being too suspicious, say: "Du er helt paranoid" (You are totally paranoid).

sentence.da: Han er **paranoid** og tror, at naboerne altid holder øje med ham.
sentence.en: He is paranoid and thinks the neighbors are always watching him.

parat.explanation: "Parat" means "ready". To say people are standing by, use it with "stå" (to stand): "Politiet står parat" (The police stand ready).

sentence.da: Er du **parat** til at gå nu?
sentence.en: Are you ready to go now?

parkeret.explanation: "Parkeret" means "parked". It comes from the verb "at parkere" (to park). To say a car is parked where it is not allowed, add "ulovligt" (illegally): "ulovligt parkeret" (illegally parked).

sentence.da: Bilen er **parkeret** foran huset.
sentence.en: The car is parked in front of the house.

parkering.explanation: "Parkering" means "parking". It comes from the verb "at parkere" (to park). To say you are looking for a space, use "finde" (to find): "Det er svært at finde parkering" (It is hard to find parking).

sentence.da: Der er gratis **parkering** bag ved hotellet.
sentence.en: There is free parking behind the hotel.

parmesan.explanation: "Parmesan" means "parmesan". Danish also has "parmesanost" (parmesan cheese), built from "parmesan" and "en ost" (a cheese).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have lidt **parmesan** på min pasta.
sentence.en: I would like a little parmesan on my pasta.

pas på.explanation: "Pas på" means "watch out". To warn someone about danger, say: "Pas på, det er varmt" (Watch out, it is hot). To tell someone to look after other people, say: "Pas på børnene" (Look after the children).

sentence.da: **Pas på** bilerne!
sentence.en: Watch out for the cars!

pas på dig selv.explanation: "Pas på dig selv" means "take care". To end a talk with a wish for the other person, say: "Tak for i dag. Pas på dig selv!" (Thanks for today. Take care!) To say it to several people, use "pas på jer selv" (take care of yourselves).

forms.da: Pas på dig selv i trafikken.

sentence.da: Farvel! **Pas på dig selv**!
sentence.en: Goodbye! Take care of yourself!

passende.explanation: "Passende" means "suitable". To say something is the right thing to do, say: "Det er ikke passende at komme for sent" (It is not appropriate to come late). To tell someone to dress for an occasion, say: "Tag passende tøj på" (Put on suitable clothes).

sentence.da: Jeg leder efter noget **passende** at tage på til festen.
sentence.en: I am looking for something suitable to wear to the party.

passiv.explanation: "Passiv" means "passive". In grammar, "passiv" names a sentence form where the action happens to the subject. For example, "Bilen blev stjålet" (The car was stolen).

sentence.da: Hun var **passiv** i timen og sagde aldrig noget.
sentence.en: She was passive in class and never said anything.

pasta.explanation: "Pasta" means "pasta". Its "the" form "pastaen" shows that it takes "en". When you talk about pasta in general, leave "en" out: "Jeg laver pasta" (I am making pasta).

sentence.da: Spaghetti er en slags **pasta**.
sentence.en: Spaghetti is a kind of pasta.

peber.explanation: "Peber" means "pepper", as in the spice. To say you season food with it, say: "Jeg bruger peber på kødet" (I use pepper on the meat). Do not mix it up with "peberfrugt" (bell pepper), a vegetable. For example, "Jeg skærer en peberfrugt i tern" (I cut a bell pepper into cubes).

sentence.da: Jeg tilføjer lidt salt og **peber**.
sentence.en: I add a little salt and pepper.

penge.explanation: "Penge" means "money". To say you have none, say: "Jeg har ingen penge" (I have no money). To talk about one coin, use "en mønt" (a coin): "Jeg har en mønt i lommen" (I have a coin in my pocket).

sentence.da: Man betaler med **penge**.
sentence.en: You pay with money.

pensioneret.explanation: "Pensioneret" means "retired". It comes from "en pension" (a pension).

sentence.da: Min far er **pensioneret** og har meget tid.
sentence.en: My father is retired and has a lot of time.

perfekt.explanation: "Perfekt" means "perfect". To agree to a plan with one word, reply: "Perfekt. Så ses vi klokken otte." (Perfect. See you at eight.)

sentence.da: Et **perfekt** svar har ingen fejl.
sentence.en: A perfect answer has no mistakes.

permanent.explanation: "Permanent" means "permanent". The opposite is "midlertidig" (temporary). For example, "en midlertidig løsning" (a temporary solution).

sentence.da: Han har et **permanent** job i en bank.
sentence.en: He has a permanent job at a bank.

persille.explanation: "Persille" means "parsley". To say it is chopped, add "hakket" (chopped): "hakket persille" (chopped parsley).

sentence.da: Jeg drysser frisk **persille** på kartoflerne.
sentence.en: I sprinkle fresh parsley on the potatoes.

personale.explanation: "Et personale" means "staff". To talk about one person who works there, use "en medarbejder" (an employee): "Vi har en ny medarbejder" (We have a new employee).

sentence.da: Sygeplejersker og læger er en del af hospitalets **personale**.
sentence.en: Nurses and doctors are part of the hospital's staff.

personlig.explanation: "Personlig" means "personal". To say a question touches someone's private life, say: "Det er et personligt spørgsmål" (That is a personal question). To say something has its own character, say: "en personlig stil" (a personal style).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **personlig** mening om det.
sentence.en: I have a personal opinion about it.

personligt.explanation: "Personligt" means "personally". To give your own opinion, put it at the start of the sentence: "Personligt synes jeg, at det er for dyrt" (Personally, I think it is too expensive). To say in person, put it after the verb: "Jeg har mødt hende personligt" (I have met her in person).

sentence.da: **Personligt** kan jeg godt lide den nye film.
sentence.en: Personally, I like the new movie.

pervers.explanation: "Pervers" means "perverted". It is a strong word, so be careful when you use it about a person. To say something is absurdly against what is reasonable, say: "Det er pervers, at vi smider mad ud" (It is perverse that we throw food away).

sentence.da: Hans humor er **pervers**, og folk bliver ofte stødt.
sentence.en: His humor is perverted, and people are often offended.

pessimistisk.explanation: "Pessimistisk" means "pessimistic". To say a person expects the worst, say: "Hun er pessimistisk" (She is pessimistic). To say a forecast looks bad, say: "en pessimistisk prognose" (a pessimistic forecast).

sentence.da: Han er **pessimistisk** og tror altid, at det går galt.
sentence.en: He is pessimistic and always thinks it will go wrong.

pinlig.explanation: "Pinlig" means "embarrassing". It describes the situation, not your feeling. To say how you feel, use "flov" (embarrassed): "Jeg er flov" (I am embarrassed).

sentence.da: Den situation var meget **pinlig**.
sentence.en: That situation was very embarrassing.

pinse.explanation: "En pinse" means "Pentecost". In Denmark, the Monday after is called "anden pinsedag" (the second day of Pentecost).

sentence.da: Til **pinse** er der en ekstra fridag om mandagen.
sentence.en: At Pentecost there is an extra day off on Monday.

piskefløde.explanation: "Piskefløde" means "whipping cream". It is built from "at piske" (to whip) and "fløde" (cream). For cream in your coffee, ask for "kaffefløde" (coffee cream): "Må jeg få lidt kaffefløde?" (May I have a little coffee cream?)

forms.en: The cake has whipping cream in it.

sentence.da: Vi pisker **piskefløde** til kagen.
sentence.en: We whip whipping cream for the cake.

pjat.explanation: "Pjat" means "nonsense". To say someone is talking nonsense, use "at tale pjat" (to talk nonsense): "Han taler pjat" (He is talking nonsense).

sentence.da: Det er noget **pjat**, og jeg tror ikke på det.
sentence.en: That is nonsense, and I don't believe it.

placeret.explanation: "Placeret" means "located". To say where a building is, say: "Biblioteket er placeret ved havnen" (The library is located by the harbor). To say someone has a high rank, add "højt" (high): "en højt placeret politiker" (a high-ranking politician).

sentence.da: Skolen er **placeret** midt i byen, tæt på stationen.
sentence.en: The school is located in the middle of town, close to the station.

pladsmangel.explanation: "En pladsmangel" means "a lack of space". It is built from "en plads" (a space) and "en mangel" (a lack). "Mangel" is also in "vandmangel" (water shortage).

forms.en: lack of space in the apartment

sentence.da: Der er **pladsmangel** i garagen, og der kan ikke stå flere biler.
sentence.en: There is a lack of space in the garage, and no more cars can fit.

planlægning.explanation: "Planlægning" means "planning". Do not mix it up with "en plan" (a plan), which is the result. For example, "Vi har en plan" (We have a plan). The work before it is "planlægning". For another example, "Rejsen kræver god planlægning" (The trip needs good planning).

sentence.da: Før festen er der meget **planlægning**.
sentence.en: Before the party there is a lot of planning.

plastik.explanation: "Plastik" means "plastic". It is also the first part of "plastikaffald" (plastic waste) and "en plastikflaske" (a plastic bottle).

sentence.da: Flasken er lavet af **plastik**, ikke glas.
sentence.en: The bottle is made of plastic, not glass.

plastikaffald.explanation: "Plastikaffald" means "plastic waste". It is built from "plastik" (plastic) and "et affald" (waste). "Affald" is also in "madaffald" (food waste).

sentence.da: Tomme flasker og poser af plastik er **plastikaffald**.
sentence.en: Empty bottles and bags made of plastic are plastic waste.

plat.explanation: "Plat" means "cheesy". When you flip a coin, "plat" is also the word for one side: "Krone eller plat?" (Heads or tails?)

sentence.da: Hans humor er **plat**, og kun få griner af den.
sentence.en: His humor is cheesy, and few people laugh at it.

pleje.explanation: "En pleje" means "care", as in looking after someone who is ill. The verb "at pleje" means "to nurse". For example, "Hun plejer sin syge mor" (She nurses her sick mother). It also means "to be in the habit of". For another example, "Jeg plejer at stå tidligt op" (I usually get up early).

sentence.da: På sygehuset arbejder hun med **pleje** af syge.
sentence.en: At the hospital she works caring for sick people.

pludselig.explanation: "Pludselig" means "suddenly". Before a noun, it means "sudden". For example, "en pludselig lyd" (a sudden sound).

sentence.da: **Pludselig** hørte jeg et højt brag.
sentence.en: Suddenly I heard a loud bang.

poesi.explanation: "En poesi" means "poetry". It can also mean a beautiful, dreamlike quality in a place. For example, "Der er poesi i den gamle by" (There is poetry in the old town).

sentence.da: I **poesi** står ordene ofte i korte linjer og med rim.
sentence.en: In poetry the words are often in short lines and with rhyme.

polen.explanation: "Polen" means "Poland". To say you are going there, use "til" (to): "Vi rejser til Polen" (We are traveling to Poland). To say you are there, use "i" (in): "Hun bor i Polen" (She lives in Poland).

sentence.da: Warszawa ligger i **Polen**.
sentence.en: Warsaw is in Poland.

politi.explanation: "Politi" means "police". To say "the police", add "-et": "Politiet er her" (The police are here). To talk about one officer, use "en politibetjent" (a police officer): "En politibetjent hjælper os" (A police officer is helping us).

sentence.da: **Politi** og ambulance er kommet.
sentence.en: The police and an ambulance have arrived.

politisk.explanation: "Politisk" means "political". To describe a debate, say: "en politisk debat" (a political debate). The subject itself is "politik" (politics). For example, "Han interesserer sig for politik" (He is interested in politics).

sentence.da: Det er en **politisk** beslutning, ikke min.
sentence.en: It is a political decision, not mine.

polsk.explanation: "Polsk" means "Polish". In English "Polish" starts with "P", but Danish "polsk" starts with "p", even for the language. For example, "Jeg taler polsk" (I speak Polish).

sentence.da: Min nabo kommer fra Polen og taler **polsk**.
sentence.en: My neighbor comes from Poland and speaks Polish.

polyester.explanation: "En polyester" means "polyester". It can start a longer word for clothes. For example, "en polyestertrøje" (a polyester sweater).

sentence.da: Mærket i trøjen viser, at den er lavet af **polyester**.
sentence.en: The label in the sweater shows that it is made of polyester.

pommes frites.explanation: "Pommes frites" means "French fries". To order them in a short way, say "pommes" (fries): "En burger og pommes, tak" (A burger and fries, please).

sentence.da: **Pommes frites** er lavet af kartofler.
sentence.en: French fries are made of potatoes.

popcorn.explanation: "Popcorn" means "popcorn". To suggest making it, use "lave" (to make): "Skal vi lave popcorn?" (Shall we make popcorn?)

sentence.da: Jeg køber **popcorn**, før filmen starter.
sentence.en: I buy popcorn before the movie starts.

populær.explanation: "Populær" means "popular". To say who likes it, use "blandt" (among): "Sangen er populær blandt børn" (The song is popular with children).

sentence.da: Det er en **populær** café, så vi bestiller bord.
sentence.en: It is a popular café, so we are booking a table.

porcelæn.explanation: "Et porcelæn" means "porcelain". To talk about the best dishes, say "det fine porcelæn" (the good china): "Vi bruger det fine porcelæn til jul" (We use the good china at Christmas).

sentence.da: Tallerkener og kopper af **porcelæn** går let i stykker.
sentence.en: Plates and cups made of porcelain break easily.

porto.explanation: "Porto" means "postage". To ask about the cost of sending something, say: "Hvad koster porto til Sverige?" (What does postage to Sweden cost?)

sentence.da: Hvor meget er **porto** til et brev til Tyskland?
sentence.en: How much is postage for a letter to Germany?

positiv.explanation: "Positiv" means "positive". To talk about good news, say: "positive nyheder" (positive news). To say a person is upbeat, say: "Hun er meget positiv" (She is very upbeat). The opposite is "negativ" (negative). For example, "et negativt svar" (a negative answer).

sentence.da: Han har en meget **positiv** holdning.
sentence.en: He has a very positive attitude.

positivt.explanation: "Positivt" means "positively". To say how someone spoke about something, say: "Hun talte positivt om projektet" (She spoke positively about the project). To tell someone to stay hopeful, say: "Tænk positivt!" (Think positively!)

sentence.da: Chefen reagerede **positivt** på forslaget og sagde ja.
sentence.en: The boss reacted positively to the proposal and said yes.

post.explanation: "Post" means "mail". To talk about mail in general, leave out "en": "Jeg har fået post" (I have received mail). It is also the first part of "et postkort" (a postcard).

sentence.da: Postbuddet kommer hver dag med **post** til os.
sentence.en: The mail carrier comes every day with mail for us.

pragtfuld.explanation: "Pragtfuld" means "splendid". It is built from "pragt" (splendor) and "-fuld" (full of). To praise a view, say: "en pragtfuld solnedgang" (a splendid sunset).

sentence.da: Fra tårnet er udsigten over byen og havet **pragtfuld**.
sentence.en: From the tower, the view over the city and the sea is splendid.

praktisk.explanation: "Praktisk" means "practical". To say it is handy to do something, say: "Det er praktisk at bo tæt på stationen" (It is practical to live close to the station). To say a person is good with their hands, say: "Jeg er ikke så praktisk" (I am not very handy).

sentence.da: Den lille taske er meget **praktisk** på ture.
sentence.en: The small bag is very practical on trips.

pressefrihed.explanation: "Pressefrihed" means "freedom of the press". It is built from "presse" (press) and "frihed" (freedom).

forms.en: freedom of the press in Denmark

sentence.da: Med **pressefrihed** må journalister skrive om politikerne uden at blive straffet.
sentence.en: With freedom of the press, journalists may write about the politicians without being punished.

prikket.explanation: "Prikket" means "polka-dotted". It is built from "en prik" (a dot). When the word after it is plural, it ends in "-e": "Hun har prikkede sokker på" (She is wearing polka-dotted socks).

sentence.da: Hendes kjole er rød og **prikket**, ligesom en mariehøne.
sentence.en: Her dress is red and polka-dotted, like a ladybug.

primær.explanation: "Primær" means "primary". To say which reason matters most, use it before the noun: "Den primære årsag er prisen" (The primary reason is the price). To say what you mostly do, use "primært" (primarily) instead: "Vi arbejder primært hjemme" (We mostly work at home).

sentence.da: Årsagen er **primær**, og de andre er mindre vigtige.
sentence.en: The reason is primary, and the others are less important.

primært.explanation: "Primært" means "mainly". To say what a shop mostly sells, put it before the goods: "Vi sælger primært brugte bøger" (We mainly sell used books). To describe a noun, use "primær" (primary) instead: "det primære mål" (the primary goal).

sentence.da: Butikken sælger **primært** brugt tøj, men også lidt legetøj.
sentence.en: The store sells mostly used clothes, but also a few toys.

privat.explanation: "Privat" means "private". To tell someone a matter is personal, say: "Det er privat" (That is private). To say who owns a place, use it before the noun: "et privat hjem" (a private home).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke tale om noget **privat**.
sentence.en: I do not want to talk about anything private.

privatliv.explanation: "Et privatliv" means "privacy". It is built from "privat" (private) and "et liv" (a life). To say someone keeps work and home apart, say: "Hun holder sit arbejde og sit privatliv adskilt" (She keeps her work and her private life apart).

sentence.da: Politikere har også ret til et **privatliv** uden kameraer.
sentence.en: Politicians also have a right to a private life without cameras.

problematisk.explanation: "Problematisk" means "problematic". It is built from "et problem" (a problem). To say something causes no trouble, use "uproblematisk" (unproblematic): "Det er helt uproblematisk" (It is completely unproblematic).

sentence.da: Det er **problematisk**, når ingen har ansvaret.
sentence.en: It is problematic when nobody is responsible.

problemfri.explanation: "Problemfri" means "problem-free". It is built from "et problem" (a problem) and "fri" (free). The ending "-fri" is also in "sukkerfri" (sugar-free) and "glutenfri" (gluten-free).

sentence.da: Flyveturen var **problemfri**, og vi landede til tiden.
sentence.en: The flight was trouble-free, and we landed on time.

produktiv.explanation: "Produktiv" means "productive". To say someone was busy but got little done, say: "Jeg var travl, men ikke produktiv" (I was busy, but not productive).

sentence.da: Hun er meget **produktiv** og skriver tre sider om dagen.
sentence.en: She is very productive and writes three pages a day.

professionel.explanation: "Professionel" means "professional". It ends in "-el", not "-al" as in English. To praise how well a job was done, say: "Det er et professionelt stykke arbejde" (That is a professional piece of work).

sentence.da: Hun er **professionel** fodboldspiller og træner hver dag.
sentence.en: She is a professional soccer player and trains every day.

protein.explanation: "Et protein" means "a protein". When you talk about protein in food in general, leave out "et": "Æg indeholder meget protein" (Eggs contain a lot of protein).

sentence.da: Kød, fisk og bønner er gode kilder til **protein**.
sentence.en: Meat, fish and beans are good sources of protein.

præcis.explanation: "Præcis" means "exactly". To give an exact amount, say: "Det koster præcis hundrede kroner" (It costs exactly a hundred kroner). To say the amount is not exact, use "cirka" (about): "Det koster cirka hundrede kroner" (It costs about a hundred kroner). To agree with someone, answer: "Så vi mødes klokken otte?" "Præcis!" (So we meet at eight? Exactly!)

sentence.da: Toget kommer **præcis** klokken otte.
sentence.en: The train arrives at exactly eight o'clock.

psykiatrisk.explanation: "Psykiatrisk" means "psychiatric". It comes from "en psykiatri" (psychiatry). To say someone is a patient of that kind, say: "Han er psykiatrisk patient" (He is a psychiatric patient). Do not mix it up with "psykisk" (mental), which is about the mind in general. For example, "psykiske problemer" (mental problems).

sentence.da: Hun blev indlagt på en **psykiatrisk** afdeling på hospitalet.
sentence.en: She was admitted to a psychiatric ward at the hospital.

psykisk.explanation: "Psykisk" means "mental". To talk about body and mind together, use its opposite "fysisk" (physical): "fysisk og psykisk sundhed" (physical and mental health).

sentence.da: Stress er en **psykisk** belastning, men kroppen mærker den også.
sentence.en: Stress is a mental strain, but the body feels it too.

publikum.explanation: "Et publikum" means "an audience". To say where someone sat, use "i publikum" (in the audience): "Min mor sad i publikum" (My mother sat in the audience).

sentence.da: **Publikum** klappede længe, da sangeren forlod scenen.
sentence.en: The audience clapped for a long time when the singer left the stage.

pudsig.explanation: "Pudsig" means "funny", in the sense of charming and a little odd. For something that makes you laugh or is fun, use "sjov" (fun) instead: "Festen var sjov" (The party was fun).

sentence.da: Hvalpen løber på en **pudsig** måde og får os til at smile.
sentence.en: The puppy runs in a funny way and makes us smile.

punktlig.explanation: "Punktlig" means "punctual". To say you arrived at the agreed time once, use "til tiden" (on time) instead: "Jeg kom til tiden" (I arrived on time).

sentence.da: Hun er altid **punktlig** og kommer aldrig for sent til møder.
sentence.en: She is always punctual and never comes late to meetings.

purløg.explanation: "Purløg" means "chives". The word "løg" (onion) is also in "hvidløg" (garlic) and "forårsløg" (spring onions).

sentence.da: Jeg klipper **purløg** ud over suppen.
sentence.en: I snip chives over the soup.

pynt.explanation: "Pynt" means "decoration(s)". It is the noun for the verb "at pynte" (to decorate). To say you buy decorations in general, leave out the article: "Jeg køber pynt til julen" (I am buying decorations for Christmas).

sentence.da: Vi hængte **pynt** op i stuen før festen.
sentence.en: We hung decorations in the living room before the party.

pyt.explanation: "Pyt" means "never mind". When someone says sorry for a small accident, answer: "Undskyld, jeg spildte." "Pyt!" (Sorry, I spilled. Never mind!)

forms.da: Pyt, det er ikke så vigtigt.
forms.en: Never mind, it is not that important.

sentence.da: **Pyt**, vi tager bare den næste bus.
sentence.en: Never mind, we'll just take the next bus.

på.explanation: "På" means "on". To say where you are at a workplace, Danish uses it for "at": "Jeg er på arbejde" (I am at work). To name a language, it is used for "in": "Jeg skriver på dansk" (I write in Danish). To say you are on an island, it is used for "on": "Vi bor på Fyn" (We live on Funen).

sentence.da: Telefonen ligger **på** bordet.
sentence.en: The phone is on the table.

på deltid.explanation: "På deltid" means "part-time". It is built from "del" (part) and "tid" (time). To name the job itself, say: "Hun har et deltidsjob" (She has a part-time job).

sentence.da: Min søster arbejder **på deltid** i en butik.
sentence.en: My sister works part-time in a store.

på den anden side.explanation: "På den anden side" means "on the other hand". To add a second view after the first, start the new sentence with it: "Huset er stort. På den anden side er det dyrt." (The house is big. On the other hand, it is expensive.) To say where a place is, it also means "on the other side": "Butikken ligger på den anden side af vejen" (The shop is on the other side of the road).

forms.da: på den anden side af vejen
forms.en: on the other side of the road

forms.da: På den anden side kan jeg vente.
forms.en: On the other hand, I can wait.

related.en: in return, on the other hand

sentence.da: Bilen er gammel, men **på den anden side** er den billig.
sentence.en: The car is old, but on the other hand it is cheap.

på den ene side.explanation: "På den ene side" means "on one hand". To start the first of two views, say: "På den ene side vil jeg gerne rejse, men jeg har ikke penge" (On one hand I would like to travel, but I have no money). To say where something is, it also means "on one side": "Haven ligger på den ene side af huset" (The garden is on one side of the house).

forms.da: på den ene side af huset
forms.en: on one side of the house

forms.da: På den ene side er det nemt.
forms.en: On one hand it is easy.

related.en: in return, on the other hand

sentence.da: **På den ene side** vil jeg rejse, men jeg er også bange.
sentence.en: On one hand I want to travel, but I am also afraid.

på forhånd.explanation: "På forhånd" means "in advance". To thank someone before they do something, end your request with: "Kan du sende filen? Tak på forhånd!" (Can you send the file? Thanks in advance!) To say you paid ahead of time, say: "Jeg betalte på forhånd" (I paid in advance).

sentence.da: Du skal booke bordet **på forhånd**.
sentence.en: You must book the table in advance.

på fuldtid.explanation: "På fuldtid" means "full-time". It is built from "fuld" (full) and "tid" (time). To say someone is drunk, the word "fuld" is also used: "Han er fuld" (He is drunk).

sentence.da: Hun arbejder **på fuldtid** og kommer hjem sent.
sentence.en: She works full-time and comes home late.

på gensyn.explanation: "På gensyn" means "see you again". It is built from "på" (on) and "et gensyn" (a seeing again). To end a visit politely, say: "Tak for i dag, på gensyn!" (Thanks for today, see you again!)

sentence.da: Tak for besøget. **På gensyn!**
sentence.en: Thanks for the visit. See you again!

på grund af.explanation: "På grund af" means "because of". To give a reason that is a noun, say: "på grund af regnen" (because of the rain). To give a reason that has a verb in it, use "fordi" (because): "Jeg bliver hjemme, fordi det regner" (I am staying home because it is raining).

sentence.da: Vi kom for sent **på grund af** trafikken.
sentence.en: We were late because of the traffic.

på tide.explanation: "På tide" means "time", as in "it is time to do something". To say it is time to act, say: "Det er på tide at gå hjem" (It is time to go home). To say something has waited too long, say: "Det er på tide!" (It is about time!)

forms.da: Det er på tide at stå op.
forms.en: It is time to get up.

forms.da: Det er på tide med en pause.
forms.en: It is time for a break.

sentence.da: Det er **på tide** at gå i seng.
sentence.en: It is time to go to bed.

på tilbud.explanation: "På tilbud" means "on sale". Literally, it is "on offer", since "et tilbud" means "an offer".

sentence.da: Kaffen er **på tilbud** i dag.
sentence.en: The coffee is on sale today.

på trods af.explanation: "På trods af" means "despite". To start a sentence with the obstacle, say: "På trods af alt er hun glad" (Despite everything, she is happy).

sentence.da: Vi tog af sted **på trods af** regnen.
sentence.en: We set off despite the rain.

på vej.explanation: "På vej" means "on the way". To say someone will arrive soon, say: "Gæsterne er på vej" (The guests are on the way). To name where you are going, add "til" (to): "Jeg er på vej til arbejde" (I am on my way to work).

forms.en: The bus is on its way.

sentence.da: Jeg er **på vej** hjem nu.
sentence.en: I am on my way home now.

påfaldende.explanation: "Påfaldende" means "striking". Before an adjective such as "stille" (quiet), it means "strikingly". For example, "Han var påfaldende stille" (He was strikingly quiet).

sentence.da: Hans tavshed var **påfaldende**, når alle andre talte.
sentence.en: His silence was striking when everyone else was talking.

pålidelig.explanation: "Pålidelig" means "reliable". To say you can count on a person, say: "Han er pålidelig" (He is reliable). Do not mix it up with "troværdig" (believable), which is about what people believe. For example, "en troværdig forklaring" (a believable explanation).

sentence.da: Han er en **pålidelig** kollega, som altid gør, hvad han lover.
sentence.en: He is a reliable colleague who always does what he promises.

pålæg.explanation: "Pålæg" means "cold cuts". It is built from "på" (on) and "at lægge" (to lay), because it is laid on bread. To name one kind, say: "Jeg vil have leverpostej som pålæg" (I want liver pâté as a topping).

sentence.da: Hvilket **pålæg** vil du have på dit rugbrød?
sentence.en: Which topping do you want on your rye bread?

påske.explanation: "Påske" means "Easter". Denmark has public holidays around it. For example, "skærtorsdag" (Maundy Thursday), "langfredag" (Good Friday) and "anden påskedag" (Easter Monday). To say you are off work, say: "Jeg har fri i påsken" (I am off during Easter).

sentence.da: Til **påske** maler børnene æg.
sentence.en: At Easter the children paint eggs.

påskedag.explanation: "Påskedag" means "Easter Sunday". The day after is "anden påskedag" (Easter Monday), and both are public holidays in Denmark. To say you visit someone then, say: "Vi besøger mormor anden påskedag" (We visit grandma on Easter Monday).

sentence.da: **Påskedag** falder altid på en søndag i marts eller april.
sentence.en: Easter Sunday always falls on a Sunday in March or April.

påtrængende.explanation: "Påtrængende" means "overpowering". To say a person is too eager and will not leave you alone, it means "pushy": "Han var for påtrængende" (He was too pushy). To say a need is urgent, it means "pressing": "et påtrængende behov" (a pressing need).

sentence.da: Sælgeren var **påtrængende** og fulgte efter mig rundt i butikken.
sentence.en: The salesman was pushy and followed me around the store.

pæn.explanation: "Pæn" means "nice", in the sense of good-looking or neat. To say a room is neat, say: "Det er et pænt værelse" (It is a neat room). To tell a child to behave, say: "Vær pæn!" (Be good!)

sentence.da: Du ser **pæn** ud i den nye kjole.
sentence.en: You look nice in the new dress.
